LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Week 10 in the NFL is here, and it's the first week where all the players who were dealt at the trade deadline will make their debuts with their new teams. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings , the Jacksonville Jaguars traded for three new defensive players, including Jordan Davis , and the Kansas City Chiefs gave Patrick Mahomes a new wideout in Josh Downs . Which one of these additions will be most beneficial for a Super Bowl run? This Sunday, the New England Patriots and Detroit Lions will battle in Germany, the Vikings and Green Bay Packers play an important divisional matchup and the Cincinnati Bengals look to steal the AFC North lead from the Pittsburgh Steelers . Which teams should you pick in Week 10, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 11 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Washington Commanders at New York Giants (-2.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Commanders +2.5): The last time these two teams faced off, they TIED. I'm expecting another close game and may be leaning toward the underdog. Washington played the Los Angeles Rams tough last Sunday and held Matthew Stafford and Co. to 20 points. J.J. McCarthy has looked solid with his new team, but he actually just became the only quarterback in the past 40 seasons to register a win with zero passing touchdowns in four straight starts (dating back to last year). He suffered a hip injury vs. the Philadelphia Eagles , while Cam Skattebo is coming off a hamstring strain. Both will play, but I do wonder how much those issues could linger. The Commanders are 4-0-1 straight up and 4-1 against the spread (ATS) in their last five against the New York Giants , so I'll take the points here in a potential upset. … Prediction: Commanders 21, Giants 20 Dubin (Giants -2.5): I don't feel particularly comfortable predicting that this Giants team will improve to 6-2-1, but I just don't have much faith that this version of Washington can be all that competitive either. The Commanders can't run the ball right now and have to lean on a passing game that hasn't been all that efficient. The Giants haven't exactly looked like world beaters this year (four of their five wins have come in one-score games), and they definitely didn't look great against the Eagles last week, but I think they can get it done on Thursday night. … Prediction: Giants 20, Commanders 14 New England Patriots vs. Detroit Lions (-2.5) (Munich) Dajani (Lions -2.5): It's going to take me some time to get over watching the Patriots have 45 points dropped on their face by the Packers. Drake Maye threw three interceptions, and the team could now be down its top two running backs. Rhamondre Stevenson is reportedly dealing with a knee injury, while TreVeyon Henderson experienced an " unusual medical emergency ." That leaves the Patriots with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison at running back. When it comes to the Lions, the question has never been about Jared Goff 's offense but about Kelvin Sheppard 's defense. No one is talking about it, but this unit has been better in recent weeks. In fact, over this four-game win streak, they rank second in points allowed per game (15.5) and yards allowed per game (286.3). Give me the Lions. … Prediction: Lions 28, Patriots 20 Dubin (Lions -2.5): The Patriots' rapidly thinning skill-position corps gives me some doubt that they can compete with the Lions offensively. Especially after New England's secondary was just lit up by the Packers, I can see Detroit having some passing game success here, bouncing back from a slow last two weeks through the air. And then Jahmyr Gibbs is always liable to go off. Drake Maye is capable of single-handedly carrying an offense against a bad defense, but as Dajani said, Detroit's defense has been playing better as of late. … Prediction: Lions 30, Patriots 21 Kansas City Chiefs (-3.5) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Chiefs -3.5): I initially wanted to take the points here with the Atlanta Falcons , but they just got home from Madrid and sent safety Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars at the trade deadline. The Falcons were dominated by the Bengals abroad, 34-17, meaning they have lost back-to-back games by at least 16 points. The Falcons' run defense will have to be ready for Kenneth Walker III , but I think the key to not getting caught by the hook could be Josh Downs, who the Chiefs acquired this week at the trade deadline. He's not some downfield perimeter threat, but is a slot weapon that could spark Patrick Mahomes' passing game. … Prediction: Chiefs 26, Falcons 21 Dubin (Chiefs -3.5): Atlanta has been getting clobbered on the ground lately (123 or more rushing yards allowed in four of the last five games and 200 or more twice) and is about to run into the Kenneth Walker train. The Chiefs finally added someone who can beat man coverage in Josh Downs, and while it might take him a few weeks to get fully up to speed, he should help them immediately in situational football. Plus, the Chiefs' defense has been really good against both the run and the pass. This line seems several points too low. … Prediction: Chiefs 27, Falcons 16 Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Dajani (Vikings +3.5): I don't know how much time Kirk Cousins is going to need to get acclimated to his (somewhat) new situation in Minnesota, but I bet this organization and this defense are JUICED to add him to the fold. Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz simply weren't cutting it, and Cousins has actually been playing some good ball out in Vegas. His 20 passing touchdowns rank second in the NFL, and his 260.0 passing yards per game rank eighth. Cousins also has chemistry with Justin Jefferson , whose 98.9 receiving yards per game when catching passes from Cousins are the most by a QB-WR duo all-time. This Packers passing attack has been lethal with Jordan Love playing MVP football and Christian Watson and Matthew Golden looking like prime Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle , but give me the Vikings to keep it close. … Prediction: Packers 20, Vikings 17 Dubin (Vikings +3.5): In-division rematches are typically lower scoring than the first matchup, so like Dajani, I see a fairly low-scoring game here despite the fact that the Packers' offense has been a fireworks show and the Vikings just upgraded their quarterback situation. These two defenses are playing extraordinarily well right now, and I think they'll be able to get a handle on what each offense is doing. In the end, I trust Jordan Love more than I do Kirk Cousins, so we'll take the Packers in a close, low-scoring game. … Prediction: Packers 17, Vikings 14 San Francisco 49ers (-3.5) at Dallas Cowboys Dajani ( 49ers -3.5): This is historically a great rivalry, but this year it's the Super Bowl favorite vs. a team that struggles with everyone they play. The 49ers have the most games missed due to injury this season (159), but that hasn't stopped them from starting 7-1. Brock Purdy 's offense scores touchdowns on 37.2% of its drives, which is the fifth-highest rate by any team since 2000! Last week's win against the Las Vegas Raiders showed how well-rounded the 49ers are, as they scored two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and a defensive touchdown. … Prediction: 49ers 30, Cowboys 26 Dubin (49ers -3.5): I don't care how many skill-position players the 49ers are missing or how old the ones that are actually healthy are: Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy are going to cut through this Dallas defense like a hot knife through butter. The Niners are so efficient on a per-play basis both on the ground and through the air, and the Cowboys make even bad offenses look competent. Dallas might be able to get something going on its side of the ball, especially if George Pickens returns to the lineup, but I don't expect it to be nearly enough to compete with what San Francisco does on offense. … Prediction: 49ers 34, Cowboys 23 Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals (-3.5) (SNF) Dajani (Bengals -3.5): I'll keep saying it, this may be Joe Burrow 's year to win MVP. He's accounted for 26 total touchdowns through eight games, while Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have combined for 47 receptions, 693 yards and eight touchdowns just over the last three games. The Bengals have scored 34 points in three straight games and 30 points in four straight games. The Steelers defeated the Bengals in Pittsburgh in Week 3, 30-27, but the Bengals will even the series on Sunday night. Cincy is 7-2 SU and ATS in its last nine home primetime games. … Prediction: Bengals 30, Steelers 24 Dubin (Steelers +3.5): I'm taking the Bengals to win, but I like the Steelers to keep things uncomfortably close. He hasn’t missed a beat with the New York quarterback changes, finding the end zone in Weeks 1, 5, 6 and 9. Yes, he scored against Washington in the overtime matchup in Week 5, catching 11 of his 13 targets for 94 yards and two scores. The Commanders have allowed eight touchdown passes to opposing tight ends in 2026 – the second-most in the NFL. At nearly 2/1, Likely is a great bet to lead this Giants offense once again in Week 10. Pick: Chiefs 23, Falcons 17 Houston Texans at Cleveland Browns (+4.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is a big game for both teams in terms of the playoff picture. The Texans looked dominant against the Chargers last week, but this is a second straight road game. It won't matter. Their defensive front will dominate whoever plays quarterback for the Browns . But the Cleveland defense will keep them in it. Pick: Texans 21, Browns 20 Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) The Packers are coming off an impressive road victory over the Patriots and Jordan Love has been on fire. But the Minnesota defense is special and now they have Kirk Cousins to play quarterback. Even so, look for the Packers to win another one as their defense limits Cousins and the offense. Pick: Packers 27, Vikings 17 Jacksonville Jaguars (-10.5) at Tennessee Titans The Titans are coming off a bye, while the Jaguars are coming off a victory last Thursday at Baltimore. They will be rested too. Jacksonville is riding high as one of the top teams in the league and made some moves at the trade deadline to get even better. Though this is a rivalry, with some unpredictable games, this won't be. Jaguars big. Pick: Jaguars 31, Titans 17 Miami Dolphins (+3.5) at Indianapolis Colts This is the dog game of the week between two struggling teams. But one is young and playing hard on the way up, while one is on the way down after trading away assets. The problem for Miami is that quarterback Malik Willis is out. That means Kyle McCord will start at quarterback. Miami will hang around against the depleted Colts team, but the Colts will win it late. Pick: Colts 23, Dolphins 22 Carolina Panthers at New Orleans Saints (-2.5) This is an enormous game in the division, even though both teams have just three victories. The winner will be in first place. The Saints beat the Browns last week, while the Panthers have lost three straight. The Saints make it four in a row as Tyler Shough has a big day. Pick: Saints 24, Panthers 21 Buffalo Bills (-8.5) at New York Jets The Bills are coming off a hard-fought road victory at Minnesota. The turnaround will be tough, but they are playing at a high level. The defense is improving. Look for Josh Allen to carve up the Jets' defense. Pick: Bills 34, Jets 21 Seattle Seahawks (-6.5) at Las Vegas Raiders Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Seahawks will start Drew Lock at quarterback again in this one. He was just OK last week against Arizona. But the Raiders have big-time defensive issues. For the Raiders, it's Fernando Mendoza time after they traded Kirk Cousins to Minnesota. This is a tough defense for a first NFL start. Look for Lock to win it as the Seahawks' defense does the rest. Pick: Seahawks 24, Raiders 16 Los Angeles Rams at Arizona Cardinals (+9.5) The Rams lost at home to the Cardinals a few weeks ago and now must play without Puka Nacua . How will they move the ball? The Cardinals will start rookie Carson Beck at quarterback. Going against Myles Garrett and company can be a problem. Rams win it, but it's low-scoring. Pick: Rams 19, Cardinals 16 San Francisco 49ers at Dallas Cowboys (+4.5) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys can't afford another loss in their division race, so this is a huge game for them. The 49ers are riding high and that offense will challenge the Dallas defense. But I think the Dallas offense will be even better. Upset special. Dak Prescott has a bigger day than Brock Purdy . Pick: Cowboys 30, 49ers 28 Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals (-3.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is for first place in the division. The Bengals are riding high behind their passing game and Joe Burrow . But the defense can't stop the run. The Steelers will run it here to keep Burrow off the field. It doesn't work. The Bengals will once again win it behind Burrow and the passing game. Pick: Bengals 27, Steelers 21 Los Angeles Chargers (+4.5) at Baltimore Ravens Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This game had promise before the season, but the Ravens are without Lamar Jackson and the Chargers are 0-8. Jacoby Brissett will start for the Ravens, which should help the offense some. The Chargers have struggled on offense, but I think their defense will keep them in this. It's close. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights John Breech predicts every Week 10 game, including a Lions victory over the Patriots in Munich Imagn Images I just got back from the NFL game in Spain, and I think I should probably start going more often, since Week 10 ended up being my best week of the year for picks. I went 14-1 straight up, and yes, I should probably just retire at this point, but I don't want to retire while I'm on top; I want to retire when I hit rock bottom, which might actually happen this week. Speaking of rock bottom, I went to McDonald's four times while I was in Spain, and let me just say, I only went there because Madrid had the nicest McDonald's I've ever seen. I mean, just look at this place. I'm now starting to understand why those Falcons players went to McDonald's. This is like the nicest McDonald's I've ever seen in my life. Wouldn't put it past Madrid to have a Michelin rated McDonald's #Bengals #Falcons #Spain https://t.co/w8WixT6iN2 pic.twitter.com/TMAeeXm9Fk There were also people tailgating inside of a Taco Bell. Taco Bell is in fact a mad house. NFL fans everywhere. Nothing like a pregame cheesy gordita crunch. #Bengals #Falcons #Spain #Madrid https://t.co/0uAafegmaM pic.twitter.com/cpjfyWy33X If you need just one reason to ever visit Spain, tailgating at Taco Bell has to be it. Unfortunately, there's no game in Spain this week, so there will be no tailgating at Taco Bell, but there is a game in Germany, and it will be the final NFL game of this year that kicks off at 9:30 a.m. ET, which is definitely for the best, because I've reached my maximum limit for 9:30 a.m. ET games. The Patriots and Lions will be playing in the early game on Sunday. So who's going to win? Let's get to the Week 10 picks and find out. Alright, now let's get to the picks for real NFL Week 10 picks Commanders (2-5-1) at Giants (5-2-1) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET (Amazon Prime) Based on everything I've seen from the Commanders , I already know exactly how this game is going to play out: Washington is going to keep this thing close until the end only to lose (or tie) because no one in the organization has any idea what to do in any key late-game situation. For instance, let's go back to Week 5 when the Commanders pulled off one of the all-time worst late-game gaffes in a tie with the Giants . Washington had the game won. All Jayden Daniels had to do was literally anything except what he actually did. The Commanders can't get the play off in time and this game ends in a tie pic.twitter.com/WmPp6q5hU0 Look at the Giants players in that clip. They're celebrating. When the other team is CELEBRATING a tie, that means you lost. Surely Daniels and the Commanders learned their lesson, right? Wrong. In their Week 9 game against the Rams , they needed a 32-yard touchdown on the final play, but instead of throwing it in the end zone, Daniels threw the ball five yards past the line of scrimmage because the Commanders apparently thought they were going to be able to lateral the ball to each other all the way into the end zone. There's a reason that never works. With the game on the line Jayden Daniels can’t get the ball out of his hand. pic.twitter.com/2D8I1YWsiA Now, you could blame Daniels for this stuff, but ultimately, it falls on the coaching staff. In the Rams' game, Daniels said he was just running the play that was called . In the Giants' game, someone on the coaching staff should have made it clear to everyone on the field that the clock has to come to a stop on that play, whether it's a spike or a player running out of bounds. So what does this mean for this game? It means that the Commanders are actually playing decent football and if their coaching staff doesn't let them down, I think they have a good chance of winning. The Giants are beat up at quarterback, they're beat up at running back, and they're surviving by the skin of their teeth. Four of their five wins have come by one score. Good teams win close games -- are you taking notes, Commanders -- and I'm starting to feel like the Giants might be a sneaky good team. To me, this is arguably the most fascinating game of Week 10. If the Commanders lose, their season is all but over, but if they win, they'll be right back in the NFC East race. I feel like this is a pick I'm going to regret as soon as I make it, but I'm taking the desperate Commanders. PICK: Commanders 24-17 over Giants Patriots (5-4) vs. Lions (6-2) in Munich Sunday, 9:30 a.m. (NFL Network) With this game being played in Munich, I feel like this would be the perfect time to answer the one question that has been on all of our minds over the past few months: Who would win a beer-chugging contest between Mike Vrabel and Dan Campbell? With these two guys heading to the beer capital of the world, there's no reason not to find out. And to be honest, based on how the Patriots have been playing recently, Vrabel could probably use a few beers right about now. I'm not in charge of scheduling events for the NFL in Germany this week, which is probably for the best, but if I were, I would rent out the Hofbrauhaus and then give both Campbell and Vrabel one full stein of beer to chug. Instead of a coin toss on Sunday, this is how we would decide who's getting the ball first. I was at the Hofbrauhaus once and it took me an hour to finish my beer. The Germans were definitely laughing at me. What's the record for most beers drank in one sitting here? I think I'm going to try to break it. pic.twitter.com/UQ5kOtxyPL The Germans might be laughing at the Patriots, too, if they can't turn things around this week. Vrabel is known as one of the smartest defensive-minded coaches in the NFL, but he hasn't figured out how to stop any NFC North teams. The Patriots have faced two NFC North teams this year and not only have they gone 0-2, but they're surrendering an average of 37.5 points per game. Yikes. The NFC North is so good that I might not pick against any of their teams for the rest of the season unless they're playing another NFC North team. If you've looked at the NFL standings at any point over the past 24 hours, you may have noticed that the NFC North is arguably the best all-around division in the NFL this year and possibly ever. All four teams are at least three games over .500, which is the first time that's ever happened through the first nine weeks. Oh, and did I mention that the NFC North is 20-4 against all other divisions. They are destroying everyone. On the other hand, you have the Patriots, who are 3-1 against AFC East opponents, but 2-3 against everyone else. The Patriots have had one of the worst passing defenses in the NFL over the past several weeks, and now, they have to face off against a QB in Jared Goff who ranks in the top five in passing yards per game this year. The Lions might put up 50 points. The good news for the Patriots is that even if the Lions do put up a 50-burger, New England might still keep up. Detroit has given up the MOST passing yards per game this year (260.9), so Drake Maye could certainly get some turkey carving practice for Thanksgiving here by carving up the Lions' defense. That being said, I've decided not to trust Maye against good teams. The Patriots have faced six opponents this year with winning records, and in those games, Maye has thrown 11 interceptions to nine touchdowns. Based on how I think this game is going to go, Vrabel might need a Hofbrauhaus beer after it's over. PICK: Lions 34-27 over Patriots Texans (3-5) at Browns (5-4) Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (Fox) Deshaun Watson did not play in Week 9 for the Browns , but there's no chance he's going to miss this game. This is the ultimate revenge, though, I can't say for sure whether this is more about the Texans trying to get revenge on him or he's trying to get revenge on the Texans. Actually, now that I'm thinking about it, there might not be any revenge involved at all here. Since trading Watson to the Browns in March 2022, the Texans have made the playoffs three times, and they've won their division twice. On the other hand, Watson has been injured for the majority of his time in Cleveland; he's won just 14 games since 2022, and the Browns have paid him roughly $14.5 million per win. If Tom Brady had earned $14.5 million per win, he would have made over $3 billion in his career. Do you know how many Hofbrauhaus beers you could buy with that money? The worst part for the Browns is that they're still in QB purgatory, which is basically where they've been since returning to the NFL in 1999. Although Watson is playing well this year, especially late in games, I'm not sure that's a good thing. If he somehow leads Cleveland to the playoffs, the Browns might actually talk themselves into re-signing him, which doesn't seem like a great idea. picks.blurb: Odds Detroit Lions Beat New England Patriots in Week 10 Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Detroit Lions travel overseas to take on the reigning AFC champion New England Patriots in Munich, Germany, on Sunday morning (9:30 a.m. EST). The Patriots, which are off to a 5-4 start, are coming off a 45-27 defeat at the hands of Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers. Meanwhile, the Lions, which are sitting at 6-2, defeated the Miami Dolphins, 19-9, in their Week 9 tilt . New England – led by Mike Vrabel on the sidelines – has lost two of its last three games, including to the Chicago Bears in Week 7. Additionally, it sits basically in the middle of the pack in both points scored (23.4/game) and points allowed (23.0/g). Yet, the Patriots still possess a myriad of talent on both sides of the ball. On offense, they're led under center by third-year passer Drake Maye, who has thrown for 18 touchdowns, 2,282 yards and a league-high 11 interceptions through nine games. He's coming off a three-interception performance against the Packers in which he completed a season-low 55.3 percent of his passes. Maye's top target this year has been veteran tight end Hunter Henry, who has amassed 32 catches, 361 yards and two touchdowns through the season's first nine games. And on the ground, the Patriots are spearheaded by sixth-year back Rhamondre Stevenson. Stevenson, a fourth-round pick of New England, has accumulated 399 yards and two touchdowns, and is presently averaging 3.9 yards per carry. Then, on the defensive side of the ball, the Patriots have received strong performances this season from the likes of EDGE defenders Gabe Jacas and Elijah Ponder, cornerback Carlton Davis III and linebacker Christian Elliss. Ponder, a second-year pro , has already recorded 7.5 sacks, eight tackles for loss and 13 QB hits, and has returned a fumble for a touchdown. And for his efforts, he's earned a 75.0 overall grade from Pro Football Focus, the 23rd-best overall grade among 110 qualified players at the position. The Patriots will not, however, have the services of Davis (knee) for this Week 10 international affair. Plus, they will also be down starting left guard Ben Brown (knee), and are expected to be without Stevenson (knee). Stevenson, the team's No. 1 back, suffered a plantaris tendon tear last week against the Packers. Those are three significant losses for Vrabel's squad going into its matchup with Detroit. As for the Lions, they will also be down multiple starters in Week 10: linebacker Jack Campbell (neck), center Cade Mays (ankle) and cornerback D.J. Reed (hip). Plus, safety Kerby Joseph, who has yet to play a single game in 2026, will not be making his season debut in Germany. While both teams are rather significantly banged up, I still believe this matchup favors Detroit. At this present juncture, I believe the Lions have a 59 percent chance to secure their fifth straight victory. They won't, however, stay in the country: their game against the Detroit Lions will take place in Munich, Germany. Perhaps unsurprisingly given their 45-27 defeat to the Packers, FanDuel Sportsbook has the Patriots listed as underdogs for that game. Odds for Patriots vs. Lions in NFL Week 10 Spread: Lions -2.5 Moneyline: Patriots +124 | Lions -146 Over/under: 50.5 The Patriots and Lions are projected to face off in a high-scoring game on Sunday. The over/under of 50.5 is tied for the highest among all New England games so far this year, and a hurdle the two teams should be capable of clearing. That said, while the Patriots have hit the over in six straight games, the Lions have not. In fact, they have not hit the projected mark three contests in a row. Obviously, there are a multiple factors that go into a game being a high- or low-scoring affair. That being said, if New England's offense and defense perform like they did against Green Bay, the scoring potential will — for better or worse — be immense on both sides of the ball. Kickoff at Munich's Allianz Arena on Sunday is scheduled for 9:30 a.m. ET. Patriots fans, join the game-day huddle! The Detroit Lions (6-2) are headed to Munich, Germany, to take on the New England Patriots (5-4) in an overseas edition of Week 10 NFL Football. It's been 11 seasons since the Lions last played an international game, but this trip has been in the works for some time. In 2024, as part of the NFL's Global Markets Program, the Lions have had marketing rights in the DACH region , which includes Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. Since then, the team has made several trips to Germany and has helped support Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown— whose mother, Miriam Brown, was born and raised in Germany —in running youth football programs across the country. As for the game itself, it looks like it'll be a good one, and the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -2.5 points . While the Lions are riding a four-game winning streak, the Patriots' 2026 season has been a more up-and-down affair after reaching the Super Bowl in 2025. They opened the season by losing to the Seahawks, beat the Steelers, then lost to the Jaguars over the first three weeks. They got back to 2-2 with a big win over the Bills, then rallied to 4-2 after wins over the Raiders and Jets. The Bears took them down on Thursday night in Week 7, but the Patriots eeked out a five-point win over the Dolphins to reach 5-3. On Sunday, the Patriots took on the Packers and looked completely unprepared. Packer QB Jordan Love jumped all over them, throwing for 372 yards and three scores, while Patriots Drake Maye threw for 299 yards and three scores, but also threw three interceptions and was sacked four times. On the ground, the Packers' worst-ranked rushing offense ran for 129 yards and two touchdowns, while the Pats gained 94 rushing yards, a touchdown, and lost a fumble. In the end, the Packers left Foxborough with a 45-27 win, and left former Patriots QB and current color commentator Tom Brady wondering who this New England team actually is: "Half the season they played like this, and the other half of the season they haven't turned the ball over, they haven't exposed the defense, have played more physical on defense, but right now it's just too inconsistent. Which team are they going to get? The team that is loose with the ball, is loose with decision-making, looking like they can be beaten by anybody. Or the team that takes care of the football, that makes the other team play left-handed, and can do what they want to do. Can they be a good team? They haven't quite done that because good teams leave the smallest margin of error." The Lions and Patriots are scheduled to play on Sunday, November 15, at 9:30 a.m. ET at Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany.

picks.blurb: 2. Not-so Super: The Patriots, just like many teams before them, haven't been able to escape the Super Bowl hangover this season. Injuries and inconsistencies are a big reason for that, but so is the drop-off in play from Drake Maye. He has already set a career-high in interceptions with 11, giving New England fans a legitimate reason to be concerned. Regardless of the situation around him, the Patriots have no chance if their quarterback can't turn it around. 3. The great outdoors: It's no secret that Jared Goff has trouble playing football when there is no roof above him. He is 1-2 in outdoor games this season, most recently defeating the Dolphins . However, Detroit's offense struggled to score points in Miami, resurfacing the questions about Goff's struggles when dealing with the elements. In fairness to Goff, he had a stellar game against the Bills earlier this season, though that did come with more ideal weather conditions. Unfortunately for the Lions, they are back outside this week in Germany and the forecast isn't as comfortable, with calls for temperatures in the 40s and 50s. Lions vs Patriots odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Lions (-1.5) Moneyline: Lions -120; Patriots +100 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Lions vs Patriots USA TODAY expert picks Adam Kaufman: Lions 30, Patriots 23 I'm more worried about who's blocking for Drake Maye than what time his alarm goes off. Will Campbell and Ben Brown both hurt their knees against Green Bay, A.J. Brown has missed two straight, and the backfield has its own injury questions with Corey Kiner in line for RB1 reps. Maye can still make enough plays to keep this interesting, especially if he gets some help back. But the Lions can put the Patriots in a bind with Jahmyr Gibbs on the ground and Jared Goff off play-action. It's hard not to trust the Lions to finish more drives after what we just watched in Foxborough. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Lions 30, Patriots 28 New England heads to Munich trying to leave its various problems stateside. Drake Maye could be in for a bounce-back performance if he can show more restraint with unforced errors. And it seems unfathomable that Christian Gonzalez could have two weeks of the kind of nightmare outing he was responsible for against the Packers . Still, Detroit's pass rush could create problems for Maye, and New England could have difficulty preventing this from turning into a shootout. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Lions 27, Patriots 21 Trusting Jared Goff to win a game without the luxury of climate control is not for the faint of heart, but the Lions are simply better at this stage. Detroit's offense, if it gets going, is something the New England can't keep up with – especially with the amount of injuries the team is dealing with. That will be the difference in Germany and Patriots fans will be left wondering if they're watching a repeat of the beatdown the Packers just gave them in Week 9. Getty The Detroit Lions will take on the New England Patriots in Germany this Sunday, giving international fans a taste of NFL action. But the Lions, who are already considerably shorthanded thanks to injuries to both Jack Campbell and Jimmy Rolder, among others, just reported a concerning update regarding quarterback Jared Goff. GettyDetroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff also delivered a heartfelt message on Dan Miller after Sunday's Week 5 victory. So far this season, Goff has been solid, throwing for 2,134 yards and 15 touchdowns with just two interceptions. During Detroit's most recent win over the Miami Dolphins , Goff completed 17 of 25 passes for 170 yards with no touchdowns. Following the retirement of Teddy Bridgewater before the season began, the Lions signed veteran Joshua Dobbs to take his place as backup quarterback. Jared Goff Spoke About Jack Campbell's Injury In Week 8, the Lions lost linebacker Jack Campbell to a frightening injury that left him hospitalized. According to Goff, after Detroit's win over the Dolphins, the Lions put forward a performance that they hope would make Campbell proud. "It was hard. It was hard," Goff said. "But I think as the week went on, you start to think about, 'What would he want? How would he want us to play?'" "He wouldn't even want us talking about him right now. He wouldn't want us doing all this stuff about how we're going to play for him. He wouldn't want any of that. But he's a special guy to us and means a lot." As Goff said, Campbell's injury had a rallying effect on the rest of the club. "I think all week, certainly early in the week, it was really hard to kind of get your mind back into what we have to do. Certainly for those guys on defense, he's their nucleus. To be able to come back to work and work the way they did, and then play the way they did, and us as a team kind of rallying around each other and leaning on each other a little bit." picks.headline: Chiefs-Falcons betting line & prediction: Will Josh Downs make instant impact?
picks.blurb: Read our AI Policy. The Chiefs acquired receiver Josh Downs, who is expected to debut Sunday in Atlanta. Patrick Mahomes practiced fully Wednesday after an elbow injury scare vs. Jets. The betting line lists Kansas City as a 3.5-point favorite over Atlanta. The Kansas City Chiefs stopped a two-game losing streak Sunday with their 35-12 win over the New York Jets to improve to 6-2. Earlier Sunday, the Atlanta Falcons lost their second straight game, falling 34-17 to the Cincinnati Bengals at Santiago Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid, Spain. The loss dropped Atlanta to 3-6. How to watch Chiefs at Falcons Kickoff: Noon Central Where: Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta TV: CBS (Channel 5 in Kansas City) Radio: KFNZ (96.5 FM in Kansas City, KNSS 98.7 FM in Wichita) Betting line: Chiefs -3.5 Behind the KC-ATL matchup The Chiefs and Falcons look a little different than they did last week, before the NFL’s trade deadline. Kansas City made the highly anticipated move Tuesday to acquire wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts . Meanwhile, Atlanta began the week by agreeing to trade three-time second-team All-Pro safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars before sending starting center Ryan Neuzil to the Baltimore Ravens. Downs is expected to make his Chiefs debut Sunday in Atlanta. He recorded 33 catches for 354 yards and a touchdown for the Colts this season. Downs’ stat line included seven catches for 72 yards against Kansas City in Week 2. “I had to watch him live. Yeah, which wasn’t good,” Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Wednesday, drawing laughter from reporters. To earn extended playing time Sunday, Downs will have to demonstrate that he can handle Reid’s complex playbook. Kansas City kept that in mind while shopping for receivers. “That’s what we felt about Josh — that he has that ability,” Reid said. “And now it’s just a matter of him spending the time to knock it out. But he’s a pretty alert kid.” How Downs fits alongside Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy will be worth watching, but the good news for the Chiefs is that his debut should come with Patrick Mahomes under center. Mahomes suffered an injury scare late in the second quarter against the Jets. Mahomes hurt his elbow but remained in the game, and medical test results were encouraging. He was listed as a full participant in Wednesday’s practice. In an encouraging development, Worthy (hamstring) also participated fully. “I feel like I’m in a great spot,” Mahomes said. “Now it’s just about pain and pain management and stuff like that, which I’ll try to do whatever I can to be in the best place possible.” While much of the focus will be on Downs’ Chiefs debut and how Mahomes attacks a Falcons secondary playing its first game without Bates, the path to victory is likely to look familiar. Running back Kenneth Walker presents a favorable matchup against an Atlanta defense allowing 4.4 yards per carry. After two less productive games by his lofty standards, Walker rushed 18 times for 102 yards against the Jets , adding four receptions for 41 yards and three total touchdowns. Following his breakout performance in Denver, rookie Emmett Johnson rushed for 34 yards and a touchdown on six carries against New York. Asked about the Falcons’ defense, Reid highlighted edge rusher James Pearce, who returned last week for 15 snaps after serving an eight-game suspension to begin the season. The former first-round pick registered 10.5 sacks as a rookie in 2025. Pearce (back) missed practice Wednesday, so his status is worth monitoring. “(The Falcons are) fast — and even faster when they’re on their turf,” Reid said. “So they’re very athletic. They’ve got some young linebackers that are flying around. They’ve got that front, and they rotate those guys.” With right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) out of practice Wednesday, Josh Ezeudu could be in line to make his second start of the season. Pearce can line up on either side of the line, and he will be a challenge for both Ezeudu and Chiefs left tackle Kahlil Benson. The Falcons feature 11 players with at least one sack, including defensive end Za’Darius Smith (4.5), defensive end Cameron Thomas (2) and defensive tackle LaCale London (2) — all with at least two sacks on the season. On offense, the Falcons’ biggest threat is running back Bijan Robinson, the only player in the league with more rushing yards (880) than Walker (872), though with one additional game. “He’s electricity in a bottle,” Chiefs linebacker Nick Bolton said of Robinson. “That’s what I say. (He’s) able to change direction, get upfield, cutbacks. We see all the time everybody’s at the point of attack because he can cut it back and put pressure on the back-side corner on the outside zone to the opposite side. So he’s electricity in a bottle, like I said, and it’ll take all hands on deck.” Much like Kansas City, Atlanta wants its running game to create opportunities through the air. Robinson’s presence helps open things up for quarterback Michael Penix Jr. and wide receiver Drake London, who leads the Falcons with 692 receiving yards but only one touchdown. The Chiefs listed cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder) as a full participant Wednesday, and his return after a two-game absence would help Kansas City match up against London. Kansas City’s defensive front will look to build on its momentum after sacking Jets quarterback Geno Smith five times last Sunday. Defensive end George Karlaftis and defensive tackle Chris Jones recorded two sacks apiece. According to NFL NextGen Stats, Penix posts a league-worst 34% completion percentage when under pressure. Jones should have an advantage over center Corey Levin, who is expected to make his first start of the season after replacing Neuzil. A sixth-round pick in 2017, Levin has spent most of his career in a reserve role. Despite kicker Harrison Butker’s recent struggles, Reid announced Wednesday that he would stick with him for now, with Justin Tucker waiting on the practice squad. Perhaps a homecoming for Butker, an Atlanta native, sparks the turnaround he’s been seeking. Chiefs-Falcons game prediction As evidenced by their respective deadline moves, the Chiefs are all in on 2026, as the Falcons look toward the future. Kansas City draws energy from Downs’ debut, Delane helps neutralize London and the pass rush builds on last week’s solid outing. away.blurb: Former Kansas City Chiefs star Mitchell Schwartz took to Twitter on November 12 to refute a report about injured offensive lineman Josh Simmons. During an appearance on 96.5 The Fan earlier in the day, ESPN writer Nate Taylor said that he hadn't seen Simmons around the Chiefs' facilities since Kansas City placed the former Ohio State Buckeye on its injured reserve list. Schwartz, on the other hand, has heard otherwise, tweeting that he had heard Simmons is "in the building" and "attacking rehab." Take a look at Schwartz's indirect refutation of Taylor's earlier report, which was posted to the All Pro lineman's Twitter account: The relative opacity that the Chiefs' front office, coaching staff, and trainers have maintained regarding Simmons' injury status will likely keep providing fodder for the rumor mill as Kansas City prepares for its highly anticipated Week 10 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on November 15. away.headline: 49ers, Chiefs pursued Garrett Wilson before NFL trade deadline
away.blurb: Wilson had also made his preference clear before the deadline, saying he wanted to remain in New York but was tired of losing . His comments reflected the frustration surrounding the team’s lack of success without suggesting that he wanted out. The New York Jets entered the NFL trade deadline as one of the league’s struggling teams, making their roster decisions a subject of interest across the league. Garrett Wilson’s name also surfaced in trade discussions, with two playoff contenders reportedly considering a move for the wide receiver. However, despite the interest, New York never seriously considered parting ways with its most important offensive player. ESPN’s Rich Cimini has now provided more details about the situation. MORE: Garrett Wilson injury: Jets have more to worry about before Chiefs game Chiefs and 49ers showed interest in trading for Garrett Wilson The Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers were interested in acquiring Wilson before the November 10 trade deadline (h/t Rich Cimini of ESPN). However, a deal was never a realistic possibility because Wilson did not want to leave, and the Jets had no intention of trading arguably their best player. New York has Wilson under contract through 2030 after signing him to a four-year, $130 million extension in 2025. The organization views the 26-year-old as a foundational piece rather than a trade asset, despite their struggles this season. MORE: Jets’ former 1st-round pick has requested trade Garrett Wilson leaves trade speculation behind but Jets face questions “I want to win games, and that’s the one thing we’ve been missing here,” Wilson said. “I love it here. Do I love it more than I love winning? Nah, to be completely honest, but I’m hopeful.” Cimini noted that the storyline could resurface in the offseason depending on how Wilson feels about the team’s direction. For now, the Jets have retained their star receiver, but they will need to give him a stronger reason to believe their fortunes can change.

away.headline: Falcons can't afford to overlook Patrick Mahomes' injury in Week 10 vs. Chiefs
away.blurb: Here's the thing though: the two-time NFL MVP is one of the best ever in terms of playing through injury. His toughness is off the charts , so it doesn't matter what he's going through, he'll be out there on Sunday afternoon. And Ian Rapoport solely referred to Mahomes' injury as an elbow strain/sprain. He said that he'll be 100% for Sunday, as both he and Andy Reid said on Wednesday they expect him to practice in full--and he did just that. All this injury will really be about is soreness and pain management since he won't miss any time, but even banged up, him being out there changes things. First, let's go over what happened to the 6-2 Chiefs in Week 9 in more detail. They blew out the Jets 35-13, behind 102 rushing yards and three total touchdowns (one rushing, two receiving) from Kenneth Walker III while Travis Kelce had a big day, catching four passes for 72 yards and a rush TD. The game-plan, especially if Mahomes hurt is going to be to get the ball out quickly, and hope they can pick up big gains after the catch against a defense that has had a problem with missing tackles this season. And whether that's Rice, Walker, Kelce, or Downs, they have the talent to stay afloat with No. 15 not at full strength. home.headline: Injured Bengals Defender Good to Go Against Falcons as Team Announces Inactives
home.blurb: Johnson was listed as questionable on the injury report with an ankle/foot designation after suffering the injury in last week’s 43-36 overtime win against the Tennessee Titans. Safety Kyle Dugger was ruled out Friday with the quad injury that has forced him to miss three of the last four games. Cornerback DJ Turner II injured his foot last week against the Titans and was limited to start the week, but he did not appear on the injury report and is expected to start and play his full role. Cincinnati Bengals defensive end Cedric Johnson is active for today’s NFL International Game in Madrid against the Atlanta Falcons. The other inactives are offensive tackle Myles Hinton, center Connor Lew and defensive tackle Landon Robinson. The Bengals only need four inactives today because their roster is currently at 52. The Bengals arrived in Madrid on Wednesday and practiced Thursday and Friday to get back on a normal weekly schedule. "I think this is the best compromise we found to make sure that we can get acclimated by Friday, get a really good practice where we feel better, and then play our best on Sunday," head coach Zac Taylor said on Thursday. "So we've all embraced that mindset, and I think it's working well for us so far." "We're back on schedule,” he added. “Our meetings were the same as they've always been on Thursday. So today is more of a third-down emphasis with some normal downs, and then tomorrow will be red zone-based." Quarterback Joe Burrow said he and his teammates are excited to be representing the NFL abroad and about being in a stand-alone window as the only game on Sunday morning. “It means a lot to me that we're here,” he said Friday. “I think this is Year 7 for me, and I haven't been overseas yet. And we keep adding more and more games to try to build the NFL globally. I think it's worked over the last five years, and I'm hoping to add more and continue to build, and I love being part of that, and I want to help grow the game, and so I love being here. "I love being the only game on TV on Sunday morning when people back home wake up, and I love showcasing our talents abroad and trying to bring attention to what we do, as far as what our offense brings. I think we're explosive, we're dynamic, we're fun to watch, and I think we're going to put on a show on Sunday." The team will fly home immediately after the game and, unlike their previous two international games when they had a bye to recover, will start preparations for a key AFC North game against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday Night Football. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Houston Texans (3-5) head to Cleveland on Sunday looking to continue a dramatic midseason turnaround when they face the Browns (5-4) at Huntington Bank Field. The Texans opened the season with four straight losses but have won three of their last four. The division may be out of reach as the Jaguars lead the Texans by three games in the AFC South but Houston is back in the race for a Wild Card spot. Cleveland takes the field after dropping their last two games which has dropped them out of first in the AFC North and 1.5 games behind the Steelers and the Bengals. Houston is coming off its most explosive performance of the season, a 44-22 road rout of the winless Los Angeles Chargers. C.J. Stroud played through an illness and completed 21 of 35 passes for 384 yards, five touchdowns and one interception. He connected with four different players for scores, including 63-yard touchdowns to Tank Dell and Kayshon Boutte , with Boutte finishing with 125 receiving yards and two touchdowns. The Texans led 24-9 at halftime, stretched the advantage to 38-9 early in the fourth quarter and defensively overwhelmed Justin Herbert , sacking him eight times. Cleveland arrives home following a gut-wrenching 23-22 overtime loss at New Orleans. With Deshaun Watson sidelined by a concussion, Shedeur Sanders started and finished 19-of-31 for 297 yards and two touchdowns, including a 64-yard go-ahead strike to KC Concepcion late in the fourth quarter. After New Orleans regained the lead, Andre Szmyt’s 51-yard field goal forced overtime. The Saints scored first in the extra period, but Sanders answered by finding Harold Fannin Jr. for a 39-yard touchdown before Cleveland went for two and the win; the conversion failed, dropping the Browns to 5-4. The matchup also renews a surprisingly balanced series. Houston leads the all-time matchup 8-7, including the postseason, but Cleveland won four consecutive meetings from 2020 through the 2023 regular season. Their most recent clash reversed that trend in emphatic fashion: in the 2023 AFC Wild Card round, Stroud threw for 274 yards and three touchdowns as Houston demolished Cleveland 45-14, with the Texans turning two Joe Flacco interceptions into defensive touchdowns. In addition to Watson’s health, other storylines include the Texans’ pass rush against Cleveland’s quarterback protection particularly after Sanders was sacked five times in New Orleans and Houston just recorded eight sacks against the Chargers. Stroud remains the player Houston needs to lead this offense. When he’s getting protection, the Texans can move the football against almost anybody. The offensive line has to keep Cleveland’s pass rush from taking over the game. Houston also needs more balance from its running attack. If Stroud has to throw on every third down, the Browns have enough defensive talent to make things difficult. Cleveland Has Been Winning Despite the Offense Cleveland is 5-4 after losing 23-22 to New Orleans on Sunday. That’s a frustrating result because the Browns had opportunities to win. They’ve been competitive all season, but the offense hasn’t been producing enough points. Cleveland has been relying heavily on its defense, and that makes every offensive mistake feel expensive. The Browns are averaging only 17.9 points and 307.8 yards per game. That’s one of the lowest scoring averages in football. Cleveland has been doing a decent job controlling possession, but it hasn’t been finishing drives. Against Houston, that’s a problem. The Texans have enough offense to create a two-score lead, and Cleveland isn’t built to play from behind. Cleveland needs better quarterback play and more production from its running game. The Browns also need their defense to create pressure and force turnovers. That’s their best chance to win. If Cleveland can keep Houston around 20 points, the Browns have a shot. But asking the offense to score 27 or 30 is a different story. It hasn’t been doing that consistently. Houston Texans vs Cleveland Browns Picks and Prediction Spread Pick: Houston Texans -4.5 I’m taking Houston and laying the 4.5 points. Cleveland has the better record, and playing at home helps. But the Browns are scoring fewer than 18 points a game. Houston is averaging more than 26. That’s a pretty big difference. The Texans just scored 44 against the Chargers, and I think they’ll carry some of that momentum into Sunday. Cleveland’s defense could make this uncomfortable, but I don’t trust the Browns’ offense to keep up. Give me Houston by a touchdown. Total Pick: Under 39.5 I’ll take the under 39.5. Houston just scored 44, so I know this looks a little strange. But Cleveland has been struggling to score, and the Browns will probably try to slow the game down. The weather shouldn’t be terrible, although the wind could make some throws more difficult. Houston can move the football, but Cleveland’s defense is capable of keeping the Texans from getting too comfortable. Something around 24-13 Houston makes sense. away.headline: Texans Injury Report vs. Browns Week 10: Multiple Starters Miss Practice
away.blurb: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans made it known that Montgomery's status has improved from last week ––when he was ruled out with a groin injury on Wednesday––but said he would continue to be evaluated throughout the week. It remains to be seen if he ends up playing once the weekend rolls around. Azeez Al-Shaair might be a name to keep an eye on, as he was a DNP with seemingly the same groin injury that's restricted his availability in practice as of late . However, given that he also had a personal designation, there's a better chance that he'll be good to go for either Thursday or Friday's session. Tight end Brevin Jordan also wound up as a DNP in practice with a finger/foot issue. If he's unable to go against the Browns, Houston has four other tight ends on the roster to turn to instead, including second-round rookie Marlin Klein, who was active on the gameday against the LA Chargers for the first time since Week 4. The Texans' final status for everyone on the roster will become clearer after Friday's practice. But until then, keep a close watch on those four who didn't practice, while also not losing sight of anyone who was limited for Wednesday’s action. Texans Final Injury Report for Week 9 vs. Chargers: Who's In, Who's Out The Houston Texans have wrapped up their first day of practice ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Cleveland Browns. And following that practice session for the Texans, we've gotten a glimpse of the injuries that this roster is dealing with in the days ahead of this weekend's contest––where in Houston's case, there's a chance that they could be forced to play without one or more of their typical starters. Let's break down the latest from the Texans' Wednesday injury report before facing the Browns in Week 10. Houston Texans Injury Report (as of 11/11) LB Azeez Al-Shaair (groin/personal) OG Keylan Rutledge (neck/shoulder) S Reed Blankenship (concussion/hand) DT Tommy Togiai (elbow/shoulder) The most notable takeaways from the Texans' first injury report of the week surround the four names who were listed as DNPs; three of them being starters. David Montgomery is the least surprising of the four, who has missed each of the Texans' team practices since leaving Week 5's game against the Tennessee Titans with a groin injury, and has gradually been working his way back to the lineup. The Texans also ended up seeing rookie offensive lineman Keylan Rutledge pop up as a rare entry on the injury report, as Coach Ryan’s noted that he had suffered a stinger during practice and would be listed as day-to-day. The stinger doesn't initially seem like something that would inhibit Rutledge's status for Sunday, but he'll have two more practices to go in order to see whether or not he'll be able to suit up. If Rutledge is indeed sidelined for whatever reason this weekend, veteran Wyatt Teller could be the primary name to look towards as Houston's next man up at left guard. He's started two games already this season in place of Ed Ingram

away.headline: Texans Injury Report: Who's Trending Up, Down for Week 9 vs. Chargers
away.blurb: Al-Shaair has been working his way back from a lingering groin injury that kept him out for Week 4's game against the Dallas Cowboys. Now, after continuing to get back to 100% from said groin issue, it seems like he's all set to play on Sunday. As for Pitre, his return to the lineup is due for a bit more attention. Pitre has been sidelined for the Texans since suffering an AC joint sprain in his shoulder against the Tennessee Titans in Week 5. David Montgomery Remains Out for Sunday Head coach DeMeco Ryans made it clear on Wednesday that David Montgomery will be missing his third-straight game this weekend against the Los Angeles Chargers. And on Thursday, he logged his second DNP of the week . Another starter who's been missing time for the Texans–– but on the defensive side of the ball–– is safety Reed Blankenship, who's missed his fifth-straight practice as a DNP, and is trending towards being out against Los Angeles for Week 9 . If Blankenship was just dealing with concussion protocol, there's a chance that if he is able to practice in limited capacity on Friday and clear protocol within 24 hours. But Blankenship is also dealing with a hand issue that might be making his return to play more complicated. home.headline: Texans Injury Report vs. Browns Week 10: Multiple Starters Miss Practice
home.blurb: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans made it known that Montgomery's status has improved from last week ––when he was ruled out with a groin injury on Wednesday––but said he would continue to be evaluated throughout the week. It remains to be seen if he ends up playing once the weekend rolls around. Azeez Al-Shaair might be a name to keep an eye on, as he was a DNP with seemingly the same groin injury that's restricted his availability in practice as of late . However, given that he also had a personal designation, there's a better chance that he'll be good to go for either Thursday or Friday's session. Tight end Brevin Jordan also wound up as a DNP in practice with a finger/foot issue. If he's unable to go against the Browns, Houston has four other tight ends on the roster to turn to instead, including second-round rookie Marlin Klein, who was active on the gameday against the LA Chargers for the first time since Week 4. The Texans' final status for everyone on the roster will become clearer after Friday's practice. But until then, keep a close watch on those four who didn't practice, while also not losing sight of anyone who was limited for Wednesday’s action. Texans Final Injury Report for Week 9 vs. Chargers: Who's In, Who's Out The Houston Texans have wrapped up their first day of practice ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Cleveland Browns. And following that practice session for the Texans, we've gotten a glimpse of the injuries that this roster is dealing with in the days ahead of this weekend's contest––where in Houston's case, there's a chance that they could be forced to play without one or more of their typical starters. Let's break down the latest from the Texans' Wednesday injury report before facing the Browns in Week 10. David Montgomery is the least surprising of the four, who has missed each of the Texans' team practices since leaving Week 5's game against the Tennessee Titans with a groin injury, and has gradually been working his way back to the lineup. The Texans also ended up seeing rookie offensive lineman Keylan Rutledge pop up as a rare entry on the injury report, as Coach Ryan’s noted that he had suffered a stinger during practice and would be listed as day-to-day. The stinger doesn't initially seem like something that would inhibit Rutledge's status for Sunday, but he'll have two more practices to go in order to see whether or not he'll be able to suit up. If Rutledge is indeed sidelined for whatever reason this weekend, veteran Wyatt Teller could be the primary name to look towards as Houston's next man up at left guard. home.headline: Browns make big Shedeur Sanders announcement for Week 9 amid Deshaun Watson's injury
home.blurb: The Browns will start Sanders, even though Watson has yet to be ruled out for Week 9. He hasn't practiced much this week, and even if he does somehow clear concussion protocol, the Browns will roll with Sanders as the starter for one week. Cleveland could give Sanders the Week 9 and Week 10 start before the team's Week 11 bye, where they could figure out who should be the starting QB for the remainder of the year. But thanks to Deshaun Watson landing in concussion protocol, there is some uncertainty at the quarterback position for this upcoming game against the New Orleans Saints . Todd Monken cleared the air on the QB situation on Friday, as Mary Kat Cabot of Cleveland.com reports that Monken announced Shedeur Sanders will be the team's starting quarterback for Week 9. Shedeur Sanders announced as Week 9 starter for Browns "Browns Shedeur Sanders will start at quarterback vs. the Saints, Todd Monken announced," Cabot reports. This is some major news for the Browns, though it isn't a huge surprise, as a player clearing concussion protocol in the same week they were put on it doesn't happen very often. Sanders will now get a prime opportunity to prove himself worthy of being the starting quarterback this season. Considering Watson hasn't exactly been playing at a super high level, Sanders could make a real case to keep the starting job in Week 9. He will go up against a very leaky Saints defense that has allowed plenty of teams to put up very big offensive days. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Week 10 in the NFL is here, and it's the first week where all the players who were dealt at the trade deadline will make their debuts with their new teams. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings , the Jacksonville Jaguars traded for three new defensive players, including Jordan Davis , and the Kansas City Chiefs gave Patrick Mahomes a new wideout in Josh Downs . Which one of these additions will be most beneficial for a Super Bowl run? This Sunday, the New England Patriots and Detroit Lions will battle in Germany, the Vikings and Green Bay Packers play an important divisional matchup and the Cincinnati Bengals look to steal the AFC North lead from the Pittsburgh Steelers . Which teams should you pick in Week 10, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 11 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Washington Commanders at New York Giants (-2.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Commanders +2.5): The last time these two teams faced off, they TIED. I'm expecting another close game and may be leaning toward the underdog. Washington played the Los Angeles Rams tough last Sunday and held Matthew Stafford and Co. to 20 points. J.J. McCarthy has looked solid with his new team, but he actually just became the only quarterback in the past 40 seasons to register a win with zero passing touchdowns in four straight starts (dating back to last year). He suffered a hip injury vs. the Philadelphia Eagles , while Cam Skattebo is coming off a hamstring strain. Both will play, but I do wonder how much those issues could linger. The Commanders are 4-0-1 straight up and 4-1 against the spread (ATS) in their last five against the New York Giants , so I'll take the points here in a potential upset. … Prediction: Commanders 21, Giants 20 Dubin (Giants -2.5): I don't feel particularly comfortable predicting that this Giants team will improve to 6-2-1, but I just don't have much faith that this version of Washington can be all that competitive either. The Commanders can't run the ball right now and have to lean on a passing game that hasn't been all that efficient. The Giants haven't exactly looked like world beaters this year (four of their five wins have come in one-score games), and they definitely didn't look great against the Eagles last week, but I think they can get it done on Thursday night. … Prediction: Giants 20, Commanders 14 New England Patriots vs. Detroit Lions (-2.5) (Munich) Dajani (Lions -2.5): It's going to take me some time to get over watching the Patriots have 45 points dropped on their face by the Packers. Drake Maye threw three interceptions, and the team could now be down its top two running backs. Rhamondre Stevenson is reportedly dealing with a knee injury, while TreVeyon Henderson experienced an " unusual medical emergency ." That leaves the Patriots with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison at running back. When it comes to the Lions, the question has never been about Jared Goff 's offense but about Kelvin Sheppard 's defense. No one is talking about it, but this unit has been better in recent weeks. In fact, over this four-game win streak, they rank second in points allowed per game (15.5) and yards allowed per game (286.3). Give me the Lions. … Prediction: Lions 28, Patriots 20 Dubin (Lions -2.5): The Patriots' rapidly thinning skill-position corps gives me some doubt that they can compete with the Lions offensively. Especially after New England's secondary was just lit up by the Packers, I can see Detroit having some passing game success here, bouncing back from a slow last two weeks through the air. And then Jahmyr Gibbs is always liable to go off. Drake Maye is capable of single-handedly carrying an offense against a bad defense, but as Dajani said, Detroit's defense has been playing better as of late. … Prediction: Lions 30, Patriots 21 Kansas City Chiefs (-3.5) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Chiefs -3.5): I initially wanted to take the points here with the Atlanta Falcons , but they just got home from Madrid and sent safety Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars at the trade deadline. The Falcons were dominated by the Bengals abroad, 34-17, meaning they have lost back-to-back games by at least 16 points. The Falcons' run defense will have to be ready for Kenneth Walker III , but I think the key to not getting caught by the hook could be Josh Downs, who the Chiefs acquired this week at the trade deadline. He's not some downfield perimeter threat, but is a slot weapon that could spark Patrick Mahomes' passing game. … Prediction: Chiefs 26, Falcons 21 Dubin (Chiefs -3.5): Atlanta has been getting clobbered on the ground lately (123 or more rushing yards allowed in four of the last five games and 200 or more twice) and is about to run into the Kenneth Walker train. The Chiefs finally added someone who can beat man coverage in Josh Downs, and while it might take him a few weeks to get fully up to speed, he should help them immediately in situational football. Plus, the Chiefs' defense has been really good against both the run and the pass. This line seems several points too low. … Prediction: Chiefs 27, Falcons 16 Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Dajani (Vikings +3.5): I don't know how much time Kirk Cousins is going to need to get acclimated to his (somewhat) new situation in Minnesota, but I bet this organization and this defense are JUICED to add him to the fold. Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz simply weren't cutting it, and Cousins has actually been playing some good ball out in Vegas. His 20 passing touchdowns rank second in the NFL, and his 260.0 passing yards per game rank eighth. Cousins also has chemistry with Justin Jefferson , whose 98.9 receiving yards per game when catching passes from Cousins are the most by a QB-WR duo all-time. This Packers passing attack has been lethal with Jordan Love playing MVP football and Christian Watson and Matthew Golden looking like prime Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle , but give me the Vikings to keep it close. … Prediction: Packers 20, Vikings 17 Dubin (Vikings +3.5): In-division rematches are typically lower scoring than the first matchup, so like Dajani, I see a fairly low-scoring game here despite the fact that the Packers' offense has been a fireworks show and the Vikings just upgraded their quarterback situation. These two defenses are playing extraordinarily well right now, and I think they'll be able to get a handle on what each offense is doing. In the end, I trust Jordan Love more than I do Kirk Cousins, so we'll take the Packers in a close, low-scoring game. … Prediction: Packers 17, Vikings 14 San Francisco 49ers (-3.5) at Dallas Cowboys Dajani ( 49ers -3.5): This is historically a great rivalry, but this year it's the Super Bowl favorite vs. a team that struggles with everyone they play. The 49ers have the most games missed due to injury this season (159), but that hasn't stopped them from starting 7-1. Brock Purdy 's offense scores touchdowns on 37.2% of its drives, which is the fifth-highest rate by any team since 2000! Last week's win against the Las Vegas Raiders showed how well-rounded the 49ers are, as they scored two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and a defensive touchdown. … Prediction: 49ers 30, Cowboys 26 Dubin (49ers -3.5): I don't care how many skill-position players the 49ers are missing or how old the ones that are actually healthy are: Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy are going to cut through this Dallas defense like a hot knife through butter. The Niners are so efficient on a per-play basis both on the ground and through the air, and the Cowboys make even bad offenses look competent. Dallas might be able to get something going on its side of the ball, especially if George Pickens returns to the lineup, but I don't expect it to be nearly enough to compete with what San Francisco does on offense. … Prediction: 49ers 34, Cowboys 23 Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals (-3.5) (SNF) Dajani (Bengals -3.5): I'll keep saying it, this may be Joe Burrow 's year to win MVP. He's accounted for 26 total touchdowns through eight games, while Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have combined for 47 receptions, 693 yards and eight touchdowns just over the last three games. The Bengals have scored 34 points in three straight games and 30 points in four straight games. The Steelers defeated the Bengals in Pittsburgh in Week 3, 30-27, but the Bengals will even the series on Sunday night. Cincy is 7-2 SU and ATS in its last nine home primetime games. … Prediction: Bengals 30, Steelers 24 Dubin (Steelers +3.5): I'm taking the Bengals to win, but I like the Steelers to keep things uncomfortably close. picks.blurb: Kirk Cousins Trade Creates Massive Shift in Vikings vs. Packers Odds for NFL Week 10 Skip to main content ON SI PREDICTION MARKETS Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Minnesota Vikings made the biggest splash in the NFL ahead of the trade deadline, acquiring veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders in exchange for a third-round pick. With former No. 1 overall pick Kyler Murray set to miss more than just Week 9 with a Grade 2 hamstring strain, the Vikings were desperate to upgrade at quarterback after falling to 6-2. Carson Wentz was awful on Monday night in a loss to the Buffalo Bills, and the Vikings couldn't afford to waste an all-time season from their defense. Cousins' acquisition impacted the Vikings' odds across the betting market. Minnesota went from +2400 to +2200 to win the Super Bowl this season at DraftKings Sportsbook , and it also jumped to -250 to make the playoffs. That's significant, as the Vikings have better playoff odds than the Green Bay Packers, Los Angeles Rams and Seattle Seahawks in the NFC. Now, with Cousins likely in line to play against Green Bay in Week 10, the Vikings are also gaining some ground in the odds for that matchup. Following Monday's loss to Buffalo, DraftKings Sportsbook had moved the Vikings to 4.5-point underdogs on the road after they opened as three-point underdogs on Sunday night. The Packers have won five of their last six games, so this was always going to be a tough matchup on the road, even though the Vikings beat Green Bay in Week 1. Now, with Cousins in the fold, the line has shifted down to Vikings +3.5 at the best betting sites . That's interesting since DraftKings is reporting that just 20 percent of the moneyline bets and 34 percent of the spread bets in this game are on the Vikings. Clearly, Cousins is viewed as a massive upgrade at quarterback for a Vikings team that enters Week 10 at No. 31 in the league in EPA/Play and No. 30 in success rate. Only the Los Angeles Chargers -- who have yet to win a game this season -- have a worse EPA/Play on offense. It's pretty shocking that the Vikings are 6-2, and they're hoping Cousins can make a quick adjustment to play in Week 10. After all, Cousins spent multiple seasons in Minnesota and has ran an offense very similar to the Vikings' current scheme at previous stops in his career. That should make it easier for him to start on a short week. This season, Cousins had led the Raiders to a 4-5 start, throwing for 2,340 yards, 20 scores and eight picks. He's not nearly as mobile as he was earlier in his career, but Cousins is certainly an upgrade over Wentz, who was unable to move the Vikings' offense in the loss to Buffalo.
