(Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images Christopher Gates · SB Nation Tue, November 10, 2026 at 2:13 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After falling out of first place in the NFC North for the first time this season, the Minnesota Vikings will look to avoid moving into the division's basement when they head to Lambeau Field in Week 10 to conclude their home-and-home series with the Green Bay Packers for this season. The people who set the betting lines, apparently, don't like their chances. Our friends at the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the lines for Sunday's game, and the Vikings currently sit as a 4.5-point underdog to the Packers. The over/under for the game currently rests at 42.5 points. The Vikings, as we all saw on Monday Night Football, appear to have completely abandoned the concept of offense, as they generated none of it in a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills for their second loss in a row. Carson Wentz stepped in at quarterback for the injured Kyler Murray and turned in what may have been the worst start a Vikings quarterback has put together in recent memory, completing just 8-of-25 passes and turning the ball over three times, including two interceptions. . .a number that could have been significantly higher. The Packers, on the other hand, have won five of their last six after getting off to a 1-2 start. This past week, they absolutely thumped the New England Patriots to the tune of 45-27 behind three more touchdown passes from Jordan Love and a defense that forced Drake Maye into three interceptions. The Packers currently sit in last place in the North, but with a 6-3 record would lead either the NFC South or the NFC East. . .that's just how good the NFC North has been this season. These two teams met in the regular season opener at U.S. Bank Stadium. Wentz came into the game midway through the first quarter after Murray suffered a concussion, and the Packers had a 22-10 lead with just over five minutes remaining in the third quarter. From there, however, the Minnesota defense took over, leading an onslaught against Love and the Green Bay offense that saw the Vikings score 29 unanswered points to finish the game, including forcing a turnover on downs and generating an interception and a fumble to set up scoring opportunities. Minnesota took home the 39-22 win to get their season off to a 1-0 start. With the NFL trade deadline looming at 3:00 PM Central today. . .or approximately seven hours from when this story goes up. . .we will see if anything the Vikings do (or don't do) will shift this number at all. As it stands now, however, the Vikings are currently an underdog to their division rivals as the second half of the season officially gets underway.

picks.headline: Packers vs. Vikings Odds: Opening line for Week 10 matchup
picks.blurb: Packers vs. Vikings Odds: Opening line for Week 10 matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL news, live updates Misiorowski, Schlittler win Cy Youngs NFL midseason awards Rex Ryan arrested Skubal suitors emerge Packers vs. Vikings Odds: Opening line for Week 10 matchup (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Justis Mosqueda · SB Nation Mon, November 9, 2026 at 6:40 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Green Bay Packers (6-3) are set to be three-point favorites over the Minnesota Vikings (6-1) in Week 10, according to FanDuel's numbers . That number comes with a little juice at -120, and the Packers are -178 favorites, which comes with an implied probability of 64 percent. If you had said this a few weeks ago, when the Packers' offensive line was drowning, no one would have bought it. Now, after Green Bay finally had a 100-yard rushing performance and beat down on the New England Patriots in all three phases of the game, it looks like the Packers have a real opportunity to make a push for the postseason. The Vikings have played two fewer games than the Packers because: 1) they've already had their bye week and 2) they're playing on Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills. After that game, they'll have a short(er) week and have to travel on the road to Lambeau Field. Their starting quarterback, Kyler Murray, is currently dealing with a hamstring injury and will not play against the Bills. We'll have to see if it heals up by the time they kick off against the Packers, or if it'll be Carson Wentz — their current replacement starter — under center. The only other quarterback in Minnesota is Max Brosmer (53-man roster). Below is the current playoff picture in the NFC: San Francisco 49ers: 7-1 (NFC West) Minnesota Vikings: 6-1 (NFC North) New York Giants: 5-2-1 (NFC East) Carolina Panthers: 3-5 (NFC South) Chicago Bears: 7-2 Detroit Lions: 6-2 Green Bay Packers: 6-3 Seattle Seahawks: 5-4 Los Angeles Rams: 5-4 Dallas Cowboys: 4-5 New Orleans Saints: 3-5 Tampa Bay Buccaneers: 3-6 Atlanta Falcons: 3-6 Arizona Cardinals: 3-6 Washington Commanders: 2-5-1 Philadelphia Eagles: 2-7 The Packers are holding onto the seventh seed right now, where they've been for weeks, but the NFC North keeps winning — as do the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams, the teams trying to hunt them down from behind. The NFC is so wonky, with the "good" teams being in the North and West, not the South and East, that the 3-6 Tampa Bay Buccaneers currently have about as good a chance of making the playoffs (by winning the NFC South) as do the Los Angeles Rams (a .500 team that is essentially locked into a playoff spot or nothing in 2026), per The Athletic's playoff simulator . In short, there are seven North and West teams fighting for five playoff spots in the NFC, and then there's whatever the hell is happening in the East and South. Do not be surprised at all if a sub-.500 NFC South team ends up hosting a 12-5 (or better record) NFC North team in the wild card round this year.

picks.headline: Week 10 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Kirk Cousins returns to lead Vikings vs. Packers
picks.blurb: Week 10 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Kirk Cousins returns to lead Vikings vs. Packers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL news, live updates Misiorowski, Schlittler win Cy Youngs NFL midseason awards Rex Ryan arrested Skubal suitors emerge Frank Schwab Senior writer Thu, November 12, 2026 at 1:48 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It wasn't that long ago that Kirk Cousins, in his first stint with the Minnesota Vikings, was the quarterback who could never win the big one . Everyone remembers this critique of him. These days, Kirk Cousins is 38. And somehow, everyone spent days and weeks arguing that the only way for the Vikings to have a chance to win the big one was to trade for Cousins. That trade did happen, and it was perfectly reasonable for the Vikings to see if Cousins can guide them to an NFC North title and maybe a playoff run. They have the defense for it but we saw on Monday night that the offense was beyond repair with the quarterback situation they had. Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell was hesitant to announce Cousins would start Sunday against the Green Bay Packers, but the Vikings didn't trade for Cousins to watch Kyler Murray or Carson Wentz start in a huge divisional game. While the trade for Cousins was reasonable, the Vikings still have the fourth-best quarterback in the division and the fourth-best offense in the division as well. Cousins is an upgrade but mostly because the Vikings had a dreadful quarterback situation. The Packers didn't do anything at the trade deadline but it might be because they've been on quite a roll. They were not good through three weeks but somehow have emerged as one of the better teams in the NFL since then. Since Week 4, they're fourth in EPA ( expected points added ) per play on offense and third in EPA per play allowed on defense. It's a good team. Anyone will have issues with the Vikings' defense and we'll see if the Packers' deep passing game can function against Minnesota's many blitzes. But Packers -3 is the pick. Taking the Vikings and Cousins, five days after rejoining the team, against a red-hot team is too much to ask. New Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins (8) shown facing the Packers in a 2023 game. Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 10 of the NFL season: Commanders (+2.5) over Giants The Giants are three games up on the Commanders in the NFC East, but New York isn't that great. The Commanders come in as the more desperate team. Their season is all but over if they lose on Thursday. That's not the best reason to pick a team, but it's good enough in a game between two flawed teams. Patriots (+2.5) over Lions This is the NFL's last early-morning game of the season. The Lions and Patriots meet in Germany. The Patriots are coming off a bad loss to the Packers, and have their running back issues with Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson out. One factor to consider is the Lions aren't the same team outdoors. Jared Goff's rating in domes is 102.9 and outdoors it is 92.4. There is some noise in those numbers, and Goff's ratings haven't had that big of a gap the past two seasons, but Detroit also just scored 19 points at Miami last week. That and the Lions' defensive deficiencies are enough to take the Patriots and the points. Texans (-4.5) over Browns The Browns have a better record, but also a -35 point differential. It's not like the Texans have been great, but there's a path for them to make the playoffs. They also know they can't drop games like this one. C.J. Stroud is playing well enough that points shouldn't be too hard for Houston to come by. Titans (+10.5) over Jaguars The Jaguars have taken over as my Super Bowl pick after the deadline. However, 10.5 is a lot of points in the NFL and the Titans have played three close games in a row. They're coming off their bye and have some extra rest. The Jaguars can't blow everyone out, right? Colts (-3.5) over Dolphins It's very hard to take the Colts, especially because the Dolphins are playing hard. The Colts played hard last week, but have to be deflated after losing that game to the Cowboys in the final minutes and seeing more players traded away. But it's even harder to back new Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord, a 2025 sixth-round pick who has never taken an NFL snap, playing with a subpar group. McCord gets the start for Miami with Malik Willis on injured reserve. Jets (+8) over Bills Talk about an ugly NFL side to take. The Jets are not good. But the Bills are coming off a physical game in Minnesota on Monday night and now go on the road to face the Jets on short rest. It seems unwise to take the Jets, but point spreads exist for a reason. Panthers (+2.5) over Saints The Saints are probably better in theory than reality. They won last week, but needed to defend a two-point conversion in overtime to knock off Shedeur Sanders and the Browns. It feels like the Saints have the potential to be the best team in the NFC South, but there's not much evidence they are. The Panthers are in a slump but have been the better team. Chiefs (-3.5) over Falcons It's not like the Falcons trading Jessie Bates III makes them significantly worse, but it's a difficult message for the locker room. It makes it seem like the front office is waving the white flag. In reality they got an offer they couldn't turn down, but it's still worth wondering how the remaining players will react. And Kansas City is a pretty good team. Cardinals (+9.5) over Rams For the rest of the season, or at least until Puka Nacua or Davante Adams returns, the Rams will try to survive by running the ball and playing defense in low-scoring games. There's not much explosiveness in the offense without any dangerous receivers. That will make them tough to back when the spread is large. Can Carson Beck lead the Arizona offense to enough points against a good Rams defense to cover any spread? That's the key question. Seahawks (-6.5) over Raiders This isn't a pick due to Fernando Mendoza facing the Seahawks defense, though that is a factor. It's because the Raiders defense is horrible. Since Week 3, after the Raiders had faced the offensively challenged Dolphins and Chargers, they're last in the NFL in EPA by a wide margin. They're 32nd in yards allowed and points allowed. The Seahawks will be able to move the ball, even with Drew Lock at quarterback. 49ers (-4.5) over Cowboys There are no signs the Cowboys are ready to have some kind of breakout. Last week they almost lost to a Colts team that has already given up on the season. And now they're supposed to keep it close against the 49ers, who have arguably been the best team in the NFL? Steelers (+3.5) over Bengals The Joe Burrow-for-MVP bandwagon is still running , but it's hard to lay more than a field goal in what should be a great divisional game. The Steelers can run the ball, and run defense is a weakness of the Bengals. They're last in the NFL in yards allowed per carry. Also, the Steelers are coming off a bye while the Bengals are coming off a game in Paris, which is the type of massive rest disadvantage that the NFL should do a better job avoiding. The Bengals are good but this isn't a great matchup or a good spot for them. Ravens (-4.5) over Chargers The Chargers will cover a spread this season. They haven't yet. They are the last team in the NFL to not cover the spread this season. But we'll take that loss when it comes because proactively taking the truly miserable Chargers in hopes they finally cover is not an enjoyable exercise. Also, the Ravens have three days of extra rest and perhaps a little bit of renewed hope with Jacoby Brissett coming aboard. Last week: 9-6 Season to date: 62-71-2

away.headline: Vikings-Bills Final Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, Kyler Murray is out as expected, as are both Demond Claiborne and Jauan Jennings. Claiborne suffered a knee injury in practice and from Kevin O’Connell’s comments on Saturday, could be out for a while. It wouldn’t be surprising therefore if he was placed on Injured Reserve. It doesn’t appear at the moment that Jennings’ calf injury is a longer-term concern, but we may learn more about that next week. Beyond that, safeties Theo Jackson and Jay Ward are questionable for Monday night. I’m guessing at least one of them will play, but KOC also talked about potentially having Jacob Thomas and/or Tavierre Thomas on the active roster for Monday night to fill in at safety and special teams. For the Bills, backup wide receiver Joshua Palmer is out. But they also have two starting offensive linemen listed as questionable- left tackle Dion Dawkins and left guard Alec Anderson. Dawkins has not practiced all week with a rib injury, so he would seem to be less likely than normal to start with that designation. Anderson was upgraded to limited on Saturday after missing Thursday and Friday practices with an ankle injury. My guess is that if either of them play on Monday night they will be less than 100%, so the left side of the Bills’ offensive line could be a bit more vulnerable than normal. Beyond that, Tyrell Shavers and Jordan Hancock are listed as questionable, but the Bills will need to activate them from the PUP list and IR for them to be eligible to play on Monday night. We’ll see if that happens. home.headline: Injury timeline emerges for Packers RB Josh Jacobs
home.blurb: Packers medical staff tried multiple methods to protect Jacobs’ hand in hopes of getting him back on the field, but he was ultimately unable to return. Jacobs will undergo surgery to repair the issue sometime later this week. According to a report from NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport, he could return to the field for the Packers as quickly as 2-3 weeks. The earliest opportunity for Jacobs’ return is a Week 12 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams. While Jacobs could be back in a couple weeks, there’s also a chance his absence extends for a longer period. If the Packers decide to place him on injured reserve this weekend, he’ll automatically be ruled out for the team’s next four games. If that’s the case, his earliest opportunity to return would be a Week 15 matchup against the Miami Dolphins. Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs fractured his ring finger during the first quarter of this past Sunday’s Week 9 win over the New England Patriots. Green Bay is set for a division-rival matchup against the Minnesota Vikings this coming weekend. After that, the team will enter its Week 11 bye. Jacobs missed the first six games of the Packers’ 2026 campaign on the Commissioner’s Exempt List. The veteran running back recorded three total touchdowns in his two full games back on the field in Weeks 7 and 8. Backup RB Kaleb Johnson stepped up following Jacobs’ exit against the Patriots, rushing for 68 yards and a touchdown on 14 carries. The Packers, led by quarterback Jordan Love, furthered their reputation as one of the best passing offenses in the league. The Packers will kick off against the Vikings at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday. home.blurb: For more from Bleacher Report, check out our B/R app , homepage and social feeds—including Twitter , Instagram , Facebook , TikTok and YouTube . Minnesota Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley hinted Kirk Cousins could potentially jump right into the starting lineup beginning with Sunday's matchup at the Green Bay Packers. Teasley told reporters Wednesday it would ultimately be up to head coach Kevin O'Connell to decide which quarterback will start when Kyler Murray is healthy. "I would leave that to Kevin, he's going to put us in the best position to succeed," Teasley said. "But we also didn't acquire Kirk to not play." O'Connell discussed the situation as well: Murray was sidelined with a Grade 2 hamstring strain from Monday's loss to the Buffalo Bills, during which Carson Wentz struggled as his replacement. The Vikings acquired Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders the following day. This article will be updated soon to provide more information and analysis.

picks.blurb: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars vs. Titans: Which New Addition Makes the First Big Play Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- After a frantic start to the week that saw the Jacksonville Jaguars make the biggest moves of this year's NFL Trade Deadline, it is worth remember that the Jaguars do, in fact, have an opponent on Sunday. The 6-2 Jaguars are set to travel to Nissan Stadium to face the Tennessee Titans in Week 10, their first game since making blockbuster trades for Jessie Bates and Jordan Davis, along with adding Davon Godchaux for a sixth-round pick. For a Jaguars team that has their eyes set on an AFC South title and a top seed in the playoffs, they are treating the Titans with the same seriousness that they treated the Indianapolis Colts and Baltimore Ravens over the last two weeks. So, how do we see the Jaguars' Week 10 battle with the Titans playing out? We break it down below. Jessie Bates Records An Interception While it certainly remains to be seen if the Jaguars will actually play any of their new defensive pieces against the Titans, I believe they will. Jakobi Meyers and Greg Newsome each played in their first games with the franchise last season after joining the team during that same week, and I think that means we see the trio make their Jaguars debuts. In the process, I think we see Bates create his first Jaguars takeaway right off the bat. Cam Ward is far from the most turnover-prone quarterback the Jaguars have played this season; that distinction goes to Daniel Jones. But he is right near the league average in interception rate, and he has made some egregious decisions with the ball over his last two seasons as a starter. This feels like the perfect week for Anthony Campanile to cook some pressure looks up to confuse Ward, and Bates is a natural playmaker. I think we see his impact right away. Parker Washington Catches 2 TDs The Titans' defense has been ... not very good against slot receivers this season. The Titans rank in the bottom-5 in the NFL against slot targets in each of the following categories: yards per play allowed, yards after the catch allowed, yards after the catch over expectation, and average seperation. The Titans have simply been a mess in the slot, even moving long-time outside cornerback Alontae Taylor to the slot despite signing him in March to play on the outside. As a result, I think this is a Parker Washington week. He is the clear No. 1 receiver in the offense, and I think he shakes off some inconsistent moments we have seen as of late and has a huge game against the Titans. Washington is due for a big performance, and I think we see it this Sunday against the Titans. Cam Ward Throws For Fewer Than 150 Yards There have been 275 quarterback performances this season. In just 39 of those performances, we have seen quarterbacks throw for fewer than 150 yards. Cam Ward makes up two of those games, a number that is trumped only by Bo Nix and Malis Willis which is, well, not great company to be in as far as productive gunslingers go. Ward has been more productive and explosive as of late and is coming off one of the best games of his career, but I predict the Jaguars limit Ward to under 150. Ward threw for just 141 yards against the Jaguars in Week 13 a year ago, and the Jaguars limited Daniel Jones and Joe Fagnano to a combined 189 yards over the last eight quarters. The Jaguars' pass defense is clicking, largely due to the work of defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile, and I believe we see it continue this week. Jaguars Limit Tony Pollard to Under 4.0 YPC Titans running back Tony Pollard has been on a tear over the last few weeks. Pollard, who has rushed for 246 yards and five touchdowns over the last two games, broke out of a mid-season skid and has been able to average over 4.0 yards per carry in every single game but two this season. While Pollard has been one of the NFL's more impressive runners over the last few weeks, I expect the Jaguars to be ready to bottle him up on Sunday. Again, I think the Jaguars will play Davis and Godchaux on Sunday. But even if they don't, I do not think the Titans have the offense to keep the Jaguars off-balance enough to run the ball on them. Teams can only run the ball on the Jaguars when the Jaguars are threatened by the early-down pass, and I do not see the Titans having much success there. Walker Little Pitches Another Shutout The Jaguars have seen Walker Little play really, really well over the last few weeks since stepping into the lineup for an injured Anton Harrison. According to NextGenStats, Little has allowed pressure on just 6.4% of his pass blocks, the fifth lowest rate in the league among left tackles (minimum 100 pass blocks). On his 109 pass blocks, his 87.2% 1-on-1 matchup rate is the highest in the league among left tackles; his 6.3% 1-on-1 pressure rate allowed is the third lowest pressure rate allowed in the league. “The experience always helps. Confidence is a heck of a thing, and I think he's the one that said it in an interview that humility helped. Where obviously he became our swing tackle, and all that guy has done is just stay the course," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said on Wednesday. "Like, never got up, too down. He's just very steady. I really like Walker's play demeanor, the look in his eye recently and not taking everything so seriously. He's able to have fun with it. He's out there playing a game that he loves and competes with, but he's playing at a high level right now. He's got confidence, and you can tell.” Little will mostly draw Titans pass-rusher Jacob Martin, who has had a good year. But after strong showings against the Houston Texans' pass-rush duo in London a month ago and then a dominant outing against Trey Hendrickson last week , I think Little has the edge entering Week 10. He is playing some of the best football of his career right now, and I predict it leads to another shutout. Cam Ward missed the majority of that game after exiting early with a shoulder injury, and his healthy showing tomorrow is the key to a potential Titans upset. The Titans falling short 36-43 in overtime was partly due to Ward taking a costly sack late in regulation, but the QB can't at all be blamed for losing a game he kept Tennessee in. The Titans even kept RB Tony Pollard at the deadline for Ward's own sake. Again, Jacksonville bulked up at the deadline - their defense specifically - but Tennessee leaving the offense untouched said loud and clear that this franchise believes in Ward. Tennessee Titans (1-7). The Jaguars have won five of their last six and are coming off consecutive blowout victories. The Titans were off last weekend but take the field having dropped two straight since recording their only victory of the season at Indianapolis back in mid-October. As is the case in most NFL games, the spotlight shines the brightest on the quarterbacks as we approach gameday. Trevor Lawrence is flourishing having thrown for 1,932 yards, 18 touchdowns and only four interceptions. He is an MVP candidate. Tennessee’s Cam Ward continues to labor under center having thrown for 1,483 yards with only six touchdowns and yet five interceptions. His future with Tennessee looks uncertain. Jacksonville’s latest performance was a convincing 33-10 Thursday-night victory at Baltimore, its second straight win by at least 23 points. Lawrence completed 16 of 26 passes for 242 yards and delivered the game’s biggest offensive play, a 50-yard touchdown to Parker Washington late in the second quarter that sent Jacksonville into halftime ahead 17-3. The Jaguars limited Baltimore to 227 total yards, forced three turnovers and kept the Ravens out of the red zone entirely; Baltimore’s only touchdown came on a 65-yard Justice Hill run in the fourth quarter with Jacksonville already leading 33-3. As noted earlier, Tennessee had its bye last week. It came at an ideal time after an exhausting 43-36 overtime loss at Cincinnati, arguably its best offensive showing of the season despite another defeat. The Titans jumped ahead 13-0 and took a 36-29 advantage with just 3:46 remaining when Ward hit Wan’Dale Robinson for a 15-yard touchdown and converted the ensuing two-point try, but Cincinnati tied the game with 1:17 left and won in overtime on Joe Burrow’s nine-yard touchdown run. Ward produced his first career 300-yard passing game, completing 26 of 40 for 304 yards and two touchdowns, while Tony Pollard ran 21 times for 117 yards and two scores. Tennessee accumulated 440 yards and forced four turnovers, including three interceptions by safety Amani Hooker , yet its defense was shredded for 510 yards and allowed Burrow to throw for 462 yards and five touchdowns before his overtime rushing score. The rivalry adds another layer because Jacksonville has emphatically reversed what was once a Tennessee-dominated series. The Titans still lead 35-28 all time, including their famous 33-14 victory over Jacksonville in the 1999 AFC Championship Game, but the Jaguars have won four consecutive meetings and seven of the last 10. Barring a miraculous playoff push without their top two defenders, rivalry points seem to be all that matter for the Titans (1-7) in Week 10 against the Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) at Nissan Stadium on Nov. 15 (noon CT, FOX). The Titans’ final nine-game stretch will be about observations. Will quarterback Cam Ward play more like a franchise quarterback to finish his second season? Will star rookies Carnell Tate and Anthony Hill Jr. maintain their pace? Who are becoming pieces for Borgonzi’s long-term vision? Finding a way to win one-score games — the Titans have lost six — can help answer those questions regardless of the team’s final record. The Jaguars have won five of their past six games and have a three-game lead in the AFC South. They enhanced their defense this week by trading for All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III from the Atlanta Falcons and 10th-year defensive tackle Davon Godchaux from the New Orleans Saints. Here’s our scouting report for the Titans’ game against the Jaguars. One Jacksonville Jaguars stat to know: 28 That’s career interceptions for Bates. He’ll be a factor. He has at least one interception in each of his nine NFL seasons. Where Tennessee Titans have edge vs. Jaguars Is Ward really the Titans’ only hope? He takes a lot of criticism, some deserved. But why can’t he be an advantage this time? He played at an elite level with a career-high 304 yards passing and two TDs against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. A Ward hot streak in November may be Tennessee’s best chance. The Jaguars rank 21st in the league in passing yards allowed per game (229.0). That’s one spot lower than Cincinnati. There’s an opportunity for Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll to give Ward more downfield throws as he did against the Bengals. Where Jacksonville Jaguars have edge vs. Titans Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence could have a big day against the Titans’ secondary, which was already leaky and now lacks its best player in Hooker. Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals shredded Tennessee with 462 yards passing, three touchdowns and nine plays of 18 yards or more. He was intercepted three times, but all of those came from Hooker. Aside from Alontae Taylor's solid debut at nickel cornerback against the Bengals, other parts of the secondary displayed poor tackling and bad angles. Tennessee ranks 31st in the NFL in passing yards allowed (258.3). Lawrence has thrown for 1,932 yards, 18 touchdowns and four interceptions. He's first in the league with 8.6 yards per pass among active quarterbacks with at least 100 dropbacks, according to Pro Football Focus. Jaguars receiver Parker Washington has 493 yards on 29 catches and is ninth among league receivers with five touchdowns. He ranks third at 17 yards per catch. Matchup to watch Titans defensive end Jacob Martin versus Jaguars left tackle Walker Little. Martin is Tennessee’s best pass rusher with Simmons gone. He had three sacks against the Bengals and has 6.5 for the season. The Jaguars have shuffled their left tackle spot this season. Little has made only three starts, but he didn’t allow a single pressure or sack in last week’s 33-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens. Score prediction: Jaguars 28, Titans 21 Ward and the Titans' offense will maintain their recent progress. But Tennessee's inability to finish games will also continue. home.blurb: This angered Ridley, and he tried to snatch the keys out of their hands, leaving a cut. Charges were attempted to be filed, and it's unclear whether they are going to be dropped or not. Ridley was also asked if he cut the person's hand after taking the keys out of their hand. He said that he didn't get to see whether he cut their hand or not. Ridley claimed that the attendant said that he broke their finger. "No, I didn't have the ticket," Ridley said. "Once you don't have your ticket, you show them your ID and fill out a form. I also showed them a picture. So, showed them more that it's my truck. My wife and kids was at the top. My mom was at the top. I came down by myself to get it. It's 11 p.m. at night. They gave me the hardest time to get my truck. I just got my keys at the registration. They wanted the registration. I gave them the registration after I got the keys. My wife came down. We got in the truck and left." Ridley was rumored to be moved ahead of the trade deadline . Nothing happened with the receiver at the end of the day. home.headline: Titans punter Tommy Townsend recounts knee injury vs Cleveland Browns | Exclusive
home.blurb: “I didn’t touch a ball for probably a week and a half before I started testing it out,” Townsend said. “Then from there it was just a very, very slow progression of (determining) how much weight I can put into my plant leg and how much weight, how much force, how hard I can swing, things like that. News Sports Counties Business Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals TITANS Titans punter Tommy Townsend recounts knee injury vs Cleveland Browns | Exclusive Tyler Palmateer Nashville Tennessean Updated Nov. 11, 2026, 5:22 p.m. CT Tennessee Titans punter Tommy Townsend returned to practice Nov. 11 after injuring his left knee. Townsend was injured during a game against the Cleveland Browns on Oct. 25. Tommy Townsend was writhing in pain and grabbing his left knee. The Tennessee Titans ' sixth-year punter didn’t know what that meant as he lay on the ground following a collision in the game against the Cleveland Browns on Oct. 25 in NFL Week 7. “I’m just happy that it (wasn’t) anything more serious,” Townsend told The Tennessean on Nov. 11. Townsend returned to practice as a full participant in Week 10 for the first time since injuring his non-kicking leg. He's also the team's placekick holder. It restores some continuity to a 1-7 team that is getting thinner by the week. The Titans have traded their two best defensive players — Amani Hooker to the Buffalo Bills and Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears — to accumulate future draft picks. Three Titans starters didn't practice on Nov. 11 as the team returned from its off week: left guard Peter Skoronski (hamstring), linebacker Cody Barton (concussion) and linebacker Anthony Hill Jr. (neck). Townsend is an All-Pro punter with two Super Bowl rings from his time with the Kansas City Chiefs. Even after missing most of the past two games, he ranks eighth in the NFL in punting average (49.2 yards), with a long of 65. "The last couple days I've been trying to swing a little harder and get back into my normal swing. The knee feels good, but like I said, it’s just getting my leg back up to speed and getting through balls like I want to.” With 1:45 remaining in the second quarter against the Browns, Cleveland blocker Sam Williams pushed Oluwafemi Oladejo into Townsend's planted left leg as he followed through on a punt. Townsend immediately fell to the turf. “Honestly, I don’t know how to explain what happened with my knee,” Townsend said. “But as you can kind of see in the clip when I was in my follow-through and coming back down, I got hit in my kicking leg. When my plant foot got put in the ground, I got hit from inside of the knee, and I guess the way I was putting force into the knee, the way it got hit, it inflamed those areas around some of the tendons and whatnot. Fortunately, wasn’t as bad as it could’ve been. MRI came back clean for the most part.” Columnist Gentry Estes contributed to this report Tyler Palmateer covers the Tennessee Titans for The Tennessean. Have a story idea for Tyler? Reach

away.headline: Where Sieler, Achane Rank Among the Most Impactful Dolphins Season-Ending Injuries of the Past 10 Years
away.blurb: Where Sieler, Achane Rank Among the Most Impactful Dolphins Season-Ending Injuries of the Past 10 Years - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Misiorowski, Schlittler win Cy Youngs Miami Dolphins defensive line Zach Sieler (92) walks off the field after the game against the Detroit Lions at Hard Rock Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Alain Poupart · Miami Dolphins On SI Thu, November 12, 2026 at 2:20 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Injuries are inevitable in the NFL, but for the Miami Dolphins unfortunately those have included this year losing two key players to season-ending injuries before reaching the halfway point. Defensive tackle Zach Sieler was placed on injured reserve Tuesday, joining running back De'Von Achane on the sidelines for the remainder of the season, Sieler with a biceps injury and Achane with a torn ACL. These were two of the most prominent players on a young, rebuilding Dolphins team already lacking in proven talent, so they're just not minimizing the impact of each loss. Unfortunately, this continues a trend of front-line players the Dolphins have lost for the season before reaching the halfway point. Over the past 10 years, you almost invariably can count on a key starter going down early, and sometimes it's more. But how do the losses of Sieler and earlier Achane compare to some of the major losses the Dolphins have suffered in the past 10 years. Here's our ranking of the top 10 most impactful injuries for the Dolphins since 2017, with the stipulation being that the injury occur in the first half of the season and based on positional value and player quality. 10. WR Will Fuller, 2021 - The Dolphins wide receiver corps in Tua Tagovailoa's second season got a boost with the addition of Jaylen Waddle in the first round of the draft, but Fuller also was supposed to help with his speed after arriving as a free agent from Houston. Instead, he sustained a finger injury in his second game with the Dolphins and never played again in the NFL. 9. G James Daniels, 2025 - Daniels was supposed to help solidify the Dolphins offensive line, but his first and only start for Miami lasted all of four plays. His absence was supposed to last a month or so, but he never came back and the Dolphins were left with trying to find an answer at right guard. 8. S Reshad Jones, 2019 - Jones easily was one of the Dolphins' best players of the 2010s and he was one of the remaining veterans on the rebuilding 2019 team, though he was done after four games. 7. CB Xavien Howard, 2019 - Similar to Jones, Howard was among those established players on that very young 2019 team, but an early knee injury slowed him down until he wound up on IR. 6. Bayou improbably tied atop the NFC South despite each having lost five of their eight games. Carolina has lost three straight after falling 26-21 to Denver, while New Orleans has won two of its last three and is coming off a 23-22 overtime victory over Cleveland. Carolina’s skid reached three games last Sunday against the Broncos, 26-21. A bright spot was the improved play of Bryce Young who completed 28 of 39 passes for 276 yards and three touchdowns with one interception. Chuba Hubbard carried the ball 16 times for 79 yards and Darren Waller caught eight passes for 90 yards. Carolina finished with 353 total yards and averaged 4.8 yards per rushing attempt but couldn’t turn that production into a win. The Panthers statistical profile underlines their issues. They average 24.9 points and 362.4 yards per game, including 261.1 through the air, but Carolina surrenders roughly 27 points per game. New Orleans comes in with considerably more momentum after surviving last Sunday in Cleveland, knocking off the Browns 23-22 in overtime. QB Tyler Shough helped erase a fourth-quarter deficit and then directed a 74-yard touchdown drive to open overtime, finishing it with a 15-yard touchdown pass to Juwan Johnson . The New Orleans defense generated five sacks, with Carl Granderson getting two. The win was the Saints’ first home win of the season. This rivalry has been remarkably competitive historically, although New Orleans has controlled it recently. The Saints swept Carolina last season and now lead the all-time series 34-29, including their lone postseason matchup. Their most recent meeting came last season on December 14, in New Orleans, when the Saints upset the Panthers 20-17 on Charlie Smyth’s 47-yard field goal with two seconds remaining. away.blurb: The Panthers designated RB Jonathon Brooks, WR Xavier Legette, and CB Mike Jackson to return from injured/reserve this week, joining OL Brady Christensen whom they designated to return last week. So the Panthers appear to be finally getting reinforcements soon, which is why I decided to devote this week’s Storylines piece to the Panthers current injury situation on both sides of the ball. The team may not get any of those 4 guys back for this week, that will be dictated by how their practices go over the coming days and how the medical staff evaluates them. So let’s take a look at their current situations on offense and defense. I’m not expecting Mike Jackson to return this week, but him being activated gives the Panthers about 3 weeks to evaluate him and decide if he’s healthy. But, there’s more good news in the secondary as Will Lee III managed a full practice on Wednesday. In addition, the Panthers finally activated Corey Thornton on Sunday, and he managed a really nice interception as the Panthers defense had a relatively okay game. I imagine Marco Wilson might get the call up once again for this secondary as well. They’ll have their work cut out for them, as the Saints have Chris Olave and now first round picks Jordyn Tyson getting more snaps coming off his injuries in the off-season. They’ll need to try their best to match up against these guys without Mike Jack and Jaycee Horn. The Panthers have spent the last few weeks without their big 2026 free agency signing Jaelan Phillips, which has greatly impacted their pass rush and the setting of the edge in the run game. He appears to be back this week after practicing in full on Wednesday coming off a hamstring injury. Its not a guarantee he will return, as those hammy injuries can pop back up, but at this juncture its promising. Which, having him return will help a defense that might be missing LB Bobby Okereke, who is still nursing the same foot injury that kept him out last week. Hello CSR! We’re on to another game week, which means we can look forward to another game of football to hopefully wipe the slate clean and get Carolina moving in the right direction again. This week, the Panthers will travel to New Orleans to face my personal most hated division rival, the New Orleans Saints. What better way to bounce back from a loss against Sean Payton’s Broncos than defeating his former team? That math maths, right? Offense: The Offensive Line is getting healthier, but can they bounce back? On top of the aforementioned Brooks, Christensen, and Legette, OG Damien Lewis practiced in full on Wednesday. He has been the Panthers best offensive linemen when healthy this season, and his presence has been sorely missed. So depending on what happens with Brady Christensen, the Panthers could have two key offensive linemen returning this week. away.headline: Panthers injury report is full of reinforcements
away.blurb: The Carolina Panthers are flailing as they try to stay afloat at the top of the ever pitiful NFC South. The team has dropped three straight games with a skeleton crew of a secondary and a revolving door of players on the offensive line. The first injury report of Week 10 brings good news though. It looks like a lot of key players are soon to return. The highlight of this injury report is all of the full participation from guys that have been out for extended periods of time. Mike Jackson, Jonathon Brooks, and Xavier Legette all had their practice windows opened on Wednesday. That doesn't guarantee that they'll be active on Sunday, but it does mean they need to be activated within the next three weeks. And the fact that they all practiced in full would suggest they're all very close to getting back to live game action. The Saints are very banged up along their offensive line. Starting center Erik McCoy is out. Both starters to his left and the backup left tackle are all dealing with their own injuries, though it doesn't seem like any will miss the game this weekend. Running back Travis Etienne is back at practice, but I wouldn't be surprised if he misses the game even after a limited practice since teams tend to be very cautious with muscle injuries like that. home.headline: Panthers vs Saints: How injuries will dictate this week’s storylines
home.blurb: The Panthers designated RB Jonathon Brooks, WR Xavier Legette, and CB Mike Jackson to return from injured/reserve this week, joining OL Brady Christensen whom they designated to return last week. So the Panthers appear to be finally getting reinforcements soon, which is why I decided to devote this week’s Storylines piece to the Panthers current injury situation on both sides of the ball. The team may not get any of those 4 guys back for this week, that will be dictated by how their practices go over the coming days and how the medical staff evaluates them. So let’s take a look at their current situations on offense and defense. I’m not expecting Mike Jackson to return this week, but him being activated gives the Panthers about 3 weeks to evaluate him and decide if he’s healthy. But, there’s more good news in the secondary as Will Lee III managed a full practice on Wednesday. In addition, the Panthers finally activated Corey Thornton on Sunday, and he managed a really nice interception as the Panthers defense had a relatively okay game. I imagine Marco Wilson might get the call up once again for this secondary as well. They’ll have their work cut out for them, as the Saints have Chris Olave and now first round picks Jordyn Tyson getting more snaps coming off his injuries in the off-season. They’ll need to try their best to match up against these guys without Mike Jack and Jaycee Horn. The Panthers have spent the last few weeks without their big 2026 free agency signing Jaelan Phillips, which has greatly impacted their pass rush and the setting of the edge in the run game. He appears to be back this week after practicing in full on Wednesday coming off a hamstring injury. Its not a guarantee he will return, as those hammy injuries can pop back up, but at this juncture its promising. Which, having him return will help a defense that might be missing LB Bobby Okereke, who is still nursing the same foot injury that kept him out last week. Hello CSR! We’re on to another game week, which means we can look forward to another game of football to hopefully wipe the slate clean and get Carolina moving in the right direction again. This week, the Panthers will travel to New Orleans to face my personal most hated division rival, the New Orleans Saints. What better way to bounce back from a loss against Sean Payton’s Broncos than defeating his former team? That math maths, right? Offense: The Offensive Line is getting healthier, but can they bounce back? On top of the aforementioned Brooks, Christensen, and Legette, OG Damien Lewis practiced in full on Wednesday. He has been the Panthers best offensive linemen when healthy this season, and his presence has been sorely missed. So depending on what happens with Brady Christensen, the Panthers could have two key offensive linemen returning this week. home.blurb: And another big one could be coming. Panthers coach Dave Canales said cornerback Jaycee Horn, a two-time Pro Bowler, is aggressively attacking his rehab but has a couple more hurdles before he’s cleared to return from his torn quadriceps injury. “My grandmother was in there, and I’m screaming the play out. They ran what I said. She said, ‘Grandson, you know what you’re talking about,’” Jackson said. “I just had to laugh it off, but inside I’m like, ‘Granny, this is not the time. I am frustrated right now.’” Since Phillips has been out, the Panthers fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero and replaced him with defensive line coach Todd Wash, who comes from more of a 4-3 background. The Panthers liked Phillips because of his experience as a 3-4 outside linebacker. But Trevis Gipson, another OLB, doesn’t think Phillips will have any issues. I don’t think he’ll have any hurdles in this defensive change. And if there are any hurdles, I’m sure he’ll fly right over them.” Jackson got a kick out of listening to Wash explain how he planned to answer Canales’ challenge to stop the run as interim DC. After a reporter rattled off the rest of the list — edge rusher Jaelan Phillips, cornerback Will Lee, guard Damien Lewis, receiver Xavier Legette and running back Jonathon Brooks — Jackson said: “I didn’t know all that.” It’s too soon to say how many in the aforementioned group will play in Sunday’s big divisional matchup at New Orleans. Because Wednesday was a light practice, Canales will have a better understanding after Thursday’s more strenuous session. Still, Wednesday felt like a win for a team that has been among the five hardest hit by injuries this season, at least according to one measure . “I’m excited about the guys that are kind of staring right at us that are gonna come back to us, in whatever order that looks like,” Canales said. home.blurb: There were two players removed from Thursday’s injury report after being listed on Wednesday: safety Justin Reid (concussion protocol) and defensive lineman Nathan Shepherd (illness). Each of the defenders now appear on track to be available for the team on Sunday. All eyes continue to be on Banks and Tyson, who could each make their way to the field sooner rather than later. While this might not be the week, Banks is inching closer to his return and Tyson moves closer to his debut. If both players do return immediately, they are in line to make consideration contributions upon being available. It appears the Saints’ offensive line could get Ruiz back after just one week of absence. If he and Banks were to both return this week, the Saints would have their offensive line at full strength for the first time since Week 2 of the season. For the Browns, the three players to keep an eye on are Watson, Collins and Fannin. With Watson trending toward not being available, the storyline writes itself with Saints quarterback Tyler Shough now set to face fellow 2025 draft classmate Shedeur Sanders instead. With Collins also headed toward at best a questionable tag, that could make a big difference for Shough with Collins tied for second on the team with 3.5 sacks on the season. The Browns have 22 total sacks this year with 12 coming from the team’s top interior players. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images MacGregor Wells · SB Nation Mon, November 9, 2026 at 1:42 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Jets lost their fourth straight game and seventh of their last eight on Sunday. The Jets are now 2-7 on the season. All playoff hopes have evaporated. In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-21 record. We are reaching Kotite-ish levels of ineptitude. This week the Jets visited the Kansas City Chiefs. They kept it competitve for a half. In the first half the Jets outgained the Chiefs. They won the turnover battle. They had more than twice the time of possession as the Chiefs. They scored on four out of five possessions. The Chiefs scored only twice. And still the Jets trailed at halftime, 14 – 12. It was an ill omen. The second half was all Chiefs. They scored 21 unanswered points and cruised to a 35 – 12 blowout over the Jets. It was just one more humiliation in a decade filled with them. The embarrassing Jets loss left the Jets with a 2-7 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season's end. Now the Jets limp home to face the first place Buffalo Bills in East Rutherford, New Jersey next Sunday. The Bills have won three straight games and six of seven on the year. Josh Allen is playing like an MVP candidate, as usual. The Bills offense is humming, leading the NFL in points scored. The Bills defense has had some issues, but they held the Baltimore Ravens to 144 yards of offense and just 10 points last week. This will be a formidable challenge for a reeling Jets team just trying to stop the bleeding. Let's take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Unsurprisingly the oddsmakers think the Bills will easily handle the Jets. The current line has the Jets home underdogs by 8.5 points. The game has an over/under of 51.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are +400 while the Bills are -520. Any given Sunday and all that jazz, but an upset here seems like a bridge too far for the Jets. Perhaps they can keep the game competitive for a while as they did against the Chiefs for a half. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Buffalo Bills (7-1) visit the New York Jets (2-7) on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium, with the AFC East rivals heading in dramatically different directions. Buffalo sits three games clear of second-place New England atop the division while the Jets have lost four in a row and sit but a half-game out of the cellar in the AFC East. The Bills enter the week with the NFL’s highest-scoring offense at 32.0 points per game and lead the league with 386.4 yards per game, powered by Josh Allen and a rushing attack featuring James Cook III . The Jets, meanwhile, are averaging just 20.2 points per game which begs the question: Can Geno Smith and the Jets score enough to keep up with the Bills’ elite attack? Working in the Jets’ favor is that Buffalo has a short turnaround after grinding out a 23-6 road victory over the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night. It was a far more physical game than the final score suggests. The Bills managed just three points on their first six possessions, and Allen threw an early interception, but his 25-yard touchdown pass to Keleki Latu with 44 seconds remaining in the first half gave Buffalo a 10-6 advantage. From there the Bills wore down Minnesota, holding the ball for an extraordinary 42:32 and running 79 offensive plays. Cook carried 31 times for 107 yards, including a five-yard fourth-quarter touchdown, while Allen finished 21-of-31 for 234 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Buffalo’s defense was even better, limiting Minnesota to 178 total yards and nine first downs while forcing three turnovers. The Jets return home after a 35-12 loss at Kansas City. Despite an early 6-0 lead, New York’s offensive woes were impossible to ignore. Smith and co. repeatedly stalled and had to settle for four Jason Sanders field goals. The Chiefs led just 14-12 at halftime before completely controlling the second half. New York finished with only 229 yards, went 2-for-12 on third down and failed to score a touchdown, while Smith completed 18 of 32 passes for 165 yards and was sacked five times. Breece Hall returned from a five-game absence caused by a quadriceps injury and produced 87 yards from scrimmage, while rookie Omar Cooper Jr. led the Jets with eight catches for 58 yards. Recent history adds another challenge for New York. Buffalo has won eight of the past 10 meetings, including a couple smacks last season, beating the Jets 30-10 at MetLife Stadium on Sept. 14, 2025 and 35-8 in Buffalo on Jan. 4, 2026. Let’s dive further into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. The model gives Buffalo a 75.1% chance to win, well below the 82.1% that -460 requires, so the Bills are overpriced. The Jets at +360 need 21.7% against a 24.9% model probability. That’s a real edge, even if it isn’t the result Bills fans are hoping for. Treat it as a small long-shot play, not a prediction that the Jets will win. Featured Prop: D.J. Moore Anytime TD (+200). FanDuel’s touchdown board is mostly overpriced, and Buffalo’s running game is the worst of it. Cook at -165 needs 62.3% against a 52.5% model probability, and Allen at -170 needs 63.0% against 58.4%. Moore is the exception: his +200 price needs 33.3%, and the model has him at 33.0%, essentially fair. If you want a Bills touchdown scorer, Moore is the one priced closest to the model. The 10,000 computer simulations project a 29-21 Bills win, close to FanDuel’s spread. The best plays are Under 50.5 at even money (+100) and D.J. home.blurb: Drafted by the Atlanta Falcons in the fourth round of the 2020 NFL Draft out of Fresno State, Walker has played for four NFL teams over the course of his six seasons in the league. The New York Jets fell to 2-7 on Sunday after suffering a 35-12 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium. New York has now dropped four games in a row and has seemingly had a very busy Monday as it sets its sights on Week 10. The Jets agreed to trade six-year safety Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions for a 2028 sixth-round pick ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. Not long after that, they made another notable roster move. Jets Sign 29-Year-Old Linebacker According to Connor Long of Jets X-Factor , the Jets are signing 29-year-old linebacker Mykal Walker to their practice squad. The move comes with Kiko Mauigoa still on injured reserve and Trevin Wallace currently dealing with an injury after missing Sunday's game against Kansas City. Walker is quite familiar with the Jets organization, as he appeared in 14 games for the team last year, primarily playing special teams and serving in a rotational defensive role. However, after roster cuts, the Jets ultimately released him with an injury settlement. NEWS: The #Jets are signing LB Mykal Walker to their practice squad, a source tells me. Walker appeared in 14 games for New York last season, contributing on defense and special teams. He was released with an injury settlement after roster cuts. — Connor Long (@connor_long15) November 9, 2026 He spent his first three seasons with the Falcons, appearing in 49 games and making 20 starts. In 2023, he joined the Pittsburgh Steelers before moving to the Washington Commanders in 2024 and ultimately landing with the Jets in 2025. Walker saw most of his production in Atlanta, but he has also made an impact with three other NFL teams. Across 88 career games and 30 starts, he has totaled 272 tackles, 14 pass deflections, eight tackles for loss, four interceptions and one sack. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Seattle Seahawks (5-4) head to Las Vegas on Sunday trying to establish some momentum in a tightly packed NFC West race, while the Raiders (4-5) are looking to rebound from one of their sloppiest performances of the season AND are looking to do so with rookie Fernando Mendoza making his first start of his career. The matchup is a monster challenge for Mendoza: Seattle has leaned on a defense allowing just 18.0 points per game, tied for fourth-best in the league entering the week, while Las Vegas has surrendered 29.8 per game, ranking last. So you expect the Raiders would look to lean on Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington Jr. to run the ball and take the pressure off their rookie signal-caller…but know that the Seahawks allow an average of 89.1 yards per game (151.2 for the Raiders). Quarterback is also a storyline for the Seahawks. Sam Darnold remains sidelined with a quad injury after also reportedly cracking a rib against Chicago, while Drew Lock came out of this past Sunday’s game dealing with an oblique issue after previously battling elbow tendinitis. Seattle comes in off a much-needed 17-3 victory over Arizona, a game it controlled despite playing without starting quarterback Darnold. Backup Lock completed 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown, while tight end AJ Barner supplied both Seattle touchdowns, catching one from Lock and running for another. Zach Charbonnet , recently returned from an ACL injury, gave the offense some balance with 77 yards on 16 carries, and the defense held Arizona to 216 total yards and no touchdowns. Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught seven passes for 51 yards and became the first NFL receiver to reach 1,000 yards this season. Las Vegas, meanwhile, is trying to clean up the turnovers after a 38-17 loss at San Francisco dropped it below .500. The Raiders were actually within 21-10 at halftime, but Kirk Cousins was intercepted on the first play of the third quarter and Jaden Dugger returned it 35 yards for a touchdown, beginning a disastrous second half. Cousins finished 22-of-32 for 216 yards, one touchdown and three interceptions as Las Vegas committed five turnovers, managed only 240 total yards and 24 rushing yards, and possessed the ball for just 21:42. Brock Bowers was possibly the only bright spot, catching seven passes for 111 yards and a touchdown. Sunday’s game is also a reunion of two franchises with considerably more history than their present-day conference alignment suggests. The Raiders and Seahawks were AFC West rivals from 1977 through 2001, and the Raiders lead the overall series 30-26, including postseason games. They have met only periodically since Seattle moved to the NFC, with the last meeting producing one of the wildest games of the 2022 season: the Raiders won 40-34 in overtime in Seattle, powered by Josh Jacobs’ 229 rushing yards and two touchdowns. away.headline: Rams’ failed trade pursuit of Chargers WR surfaces after NFL trade deadline
away.blurb: “Overall, though, the Rams didn’t seriously consider a receiver move because they expect both Puka Nacua and Davante Adams to return this season,” he added. The Los Angeles Rams did not complete a major trade before Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, despite their wide receiver room being decimated by injuries. But ESPN insider Dan Graziano reported that Los Angeles kicked the tires on a potential blockbuster deal for a cross-town receiver. “The Chargers said no to at least one Ladd McConkey inquiry. Teams I spoke to believe the Rams were the ones to make that call,” Graziano wrote on Wednesday. The Rams trading for Los Angeles Chargers star receiver Ladd McConkey would have been one of the biggest trades made this season, despite McConkey’s disappointing campaign. The 24-year-old former Georgia Bulldogs star has 17 receptions for 286 receiving yards and one touchdown this season. That output leaves a lot to be desired, but the 0-8 Chargers’ entire offense has been abysmal, and McConkey’s production has taken a hit as a result. Not that it matters now, as the trade chatter reportedly didn’t make it far. The Chargers’ refusal to consider trading McConkey suggests they still see him as a key part of their future. Whether that thinking was wise remains to be seen.

home.headline: Cardinals QB situation takes stunning turn with Gardner Minshew update: report
home.blurb: Following their 17-3 road loss Sunday to the Seattle Seahawks, the Arizona Cardinals received a major update on quarterback Gardner Minshew, who may have suffered a season-ending injury. On Monday evening, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that Minshew “is feared to have suffered a torn UCL in his throwing arm.” Rapoport said Minshew suffered the injury before halftime but continued playing through it. According to Rapoport, Minshew will get additional testing done, but the injury could end his season and require a lengthy rehabilitation process. Minshew suffered the injury when he was hit by Seahawks pass rusher Dante Fowler while attempting a pass on the final play of the first half. The Cardinals quarterback grabbed his right arm after the rough hit, but continued to play. In Sunday’s game, Minshew completed 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards and was sacked three times by the Seahawks defense. Seattle held Arizona to just 198 total yards of offense for the game. More news: Chiefs HC Andy Reid Reveals Patrick Mahomes Injury Update Ahead of Falcons Game The devastating update arrived days after the team traded veteran starter Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens. Arizona’s unfortunate situation with Minshew has led to several developments, including Adam Schefter reporting that the team signed Josh Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals’ practice squad. This is Johnson’s 15th team in 14 seasons. According to ESPN , in an initial report on the Cardinals’ injury updates, rookie Carson Beck was expected to start on Sunday. The Cardinals drafted the former Miami Hurricanes quarterback at No. 65 in the 3rd round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Beck led his team to the College Football Playoff National Championship game, which they lost to Fernando Mendoza and the Indiana Hoosiers. The decision to draft Beck was met with mixed reviews, with many sports outlets giving the team a low grade for the pick. NFL.com’s Chad Reuter graded Arizona’s Day 2 picks, including Beck, an “A,” indicating he had “a lot of big-game experience.” However, Reuter also noted that Beck’s decision-making was too inconsistent to be a “surefire starter.” Beck appeared in the NFL Hall of Fame Game this preseason against the Carolina Panthers, throwing for 188 yards and a touchdown in Arizona’s 33-30 loss. With ESPN reporting that Beck is expected to start Sunday, he’s poised to take over for a 3-6 Arizona team, unless they opt to use Johnson instead. Unfortunately, both quarterbacks could face a challenging matchup for the team’s next NFL game. The Cardinals host a Los Angeles Rams team on Sunday, Nov. 15, that has now won three straight games to improve to 5-4 for the season. The Rams also just got back the NFL Defensive Player of the Year, Myles Garrett, who recorded three sacks on Sunday in their 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders, so Beck or Johnson could face a difficult test for his first NFL start. Five weeks after Arizona stunned Los Angeles with an 18-16 walk-off victory at SoFi Stadium, the NFC West rivals reunite Sunday at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Ariz., for a rematch that could determine whether the Rams enter their bye week riding a four-game winning streak or reliving their most embarrassing loss of the season. Now the Rams (5-4) want revenge. Unfortunately, they're bringing what amounts to a skeleton crew to the battlefield. home.headline: Cardinals Forced to Sign 40-Year-Old QB as Injuries Mount
home.blurb: “I think probably even stronger than how I said it yesterday. I wasn’t anticipating some of the things that we found out today. I knew that particularly on offense — (with) the defense there’s been a guy here and there, but there’s been some decent continuity over the last month, and I think you guys see that," LaFleur said. Cardinals Coach Said The Quiet Part Out Loud on Carson Beck ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals' Monday has taken a steep twist thanks to several significant injuries to their offense, and with news of Gardner Minshew potentially being done for the season, the organization has already targeted their next passer. From ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter: "With veteran QB Gardner Minshew sidelined due to a UCL injury, the Cardinals are signing QB Josh Johnson off the Bengals’ practice squad, per sources. The Cardinals will be Johnson’s 15th NFL team in 14 NFL seasons." Johnson, a perennial backup veteran quarterback, will be the team's No. 2 quarterback as the Cardinals prepare for their Week 10 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams — who just welcomed Myles Garrett back to the mix with a three-sack performance this Sunday. Minshew was injured on the final play of the second quarter against Seattle. He returned to finish the game but showed obvious discomfort. Rookie quarterback Carson Beck is slated to start for Arizona this week. Johnson, 40 years old, first entered the league as a fifth-round pick in the 2008 NFL Draft. He's played 50 NFL games with 11 starts, most recently starting twice for the Washington Commanders in 2025. In those two games, Johnson completed 34 of 54 passes for 372 yards for one touchdown and two interceptions. He has a 2-9 record as a starter. It was an extremely tough day for the Cardinals, who lost both Minshew and Michael Wilson . Arizona head coach Mike LaFleur says the team has to regroup, even amid the injuries. "I think you see 11 has won more and more each week, particularly over these last four weeks. Not the case on offense right now and that’s what I meant by that. There’s been a lot of moving parts, and I have to do a better job of stabilizing that to make sure that we don’t have performances like we did yesterday.” The Cardinals recently dealt Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens last week, thinning their quarterback room down to two. With Minshew injured, Beck was the only healthy quarterback on the roster prior to Johnson's signing. home.blurb: Rams-Cardinals injury report: McDuffie, Curl and Ferguson DNP Wednesday - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Rams-Cardinals injury report: McDuffie, Curl and Ferguson DNP Wednesday To start the week, the Rams listed 10 players on their initial injury report, five of whom did not practice at all. The Rams only held a walk-through, so participation is an estimate. Trent McDuffie, Kam Curl and Terrance Ferguson were all non-participants. Sean McVay said the Rams are "optimistic" McDuffie will be able to play on Sunday, which is a good sign despite his absence Wednesday. Curl played last week after being questionable with a foot injury, but he's now listed with a toe injury. Ferguson is dealing with a hamstring injury after pulling it in practice last week. He's still on IR but can be activated at any time. Colby Parkinson continues to battle a rib injury, but it's encouraging that he was at least limited on Wednesday. Joe Cardona could be making progress with his ankle injury, too. Myles Garrett continues to nurse his knee injury and Davis Allen has an oblique injury that forced him to be limited. On the Cardinals' injury report, Budda Baker had a rest day, and Hjalte Froholdt missed practice while recovering from a concussion. Bam Knight is still progressing through the concussion protocol and was limited in practice. Josh Sweat and Isaac Seumalo both got veteran rest days, too. They have one game left before their bye, as they'll visit the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday in an attempt to avenge their shocking Week 6 loss to their division rival. The Rams still haven't overcome the injuries suffered in that game, remaining without Davante Adams, Kobie Turner and Poona Ford, but the Cardinals are in much worse shape. They're without Jeremiyah Love and now Michael Wilson, while Jacoby Brissett has been traded and his replacement, Gardner Minshew, is injured, too. picks.headline: 49ers vs. Cowboys bold predictions for NFL Week 10
picks.blurb: 49ers vs. Cowboys bold predictions for NFL Week 10 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL news, live updates Misiorowski, Schlittler win Cy Youngs NFL midseason awards Rex Ryan arrested Skubal suitors emerge 49ers vs. Cowboys bold predictions for NFL Week 10 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 10, 2026 at 11:03 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads While the San Francisco 49ers made a fairly mild move, the Dallas Cowboys didn't move the needle at the trade deadline. But these teams meet in Week 10 of the NFL season, and here are bold predictions for the contest. Entering with a record of 7-1, the 49ers sit as the No. 1 in the NFC. Meanwhile, the Cowboys are trying to fight their way back into contention in the NFC East. They have a record of 4-5. The 49ers are road favorites, but only by 3.5 points. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) 49ers QB Brock Purdy will throw for 250 yards and two TD passes It's a matter of scheme that Purdy will have success , according to ESPN. "Kyle Shanahan will have answers for both the run and pass game Sunday in Dallas," Matt Bowen wrote. "Schemed throws for Brock Purdy that create open coverage voids off play-action, plus a multiple run game with Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black to attack a Cowboys defense, allowing 5.0 YPC (third most). I like the 49ers to cover on the road." Purdy has thrown for 1,980 yards this season with 17 touchdowns and five interceptions. He has been impressive and has the eye of head coach Kyle Shanahan, according to a post on X by 95.7 TheGame via Heavy.com. "Yeah, it's been amazing," Shanahan said. "Just since the first game he got in there. That's why I struggle at the beginning of the year when everyone's asking me, can I believe how good he's playing and how much better he's improved because he was so good off the bench versus Miami in his first game and the second week… taking us to the NFC Championship as a rookie. "And I think his second year took us to the Super Bowl maybe. So Brock's been the man since he's come in, and it's pretty unbelievable deal considering where he was drafted, how he started… very fortunate to have Brock." The Cowboys will have their hands full. Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb will get 8-plus catches and 90-plus yards The Cowboys are going to get the ball to Lamb. It's their best path to having a shot at beating the 49ers. Lamb left the win over the Colts with a sigh of relief, according to dallascowboys.com. "Those are the games that you love to end up on top," Lamb said. "We understand it was the same situation that we were kind of in last week, and we didn't end up on top then, so just finishing out the game, finishing out the drive — shout out to the defense for ending the game. "But I think I had, like, three penalties alone in the second half, and a fumble. Personally, I gotta take a real good look. The numbers look crazy, but it could have been more. And I'm always thinking about what could have been. So, as for me, as a leader on this offense,I feel like I've got to be better in some realms and just end the game." The 49ers are off to a great start. But before the season, the Cowboys were in the same conversation with them. Lamb said the Cowboys need to get the job done. "We know what we got going on, just the history of that [matchup], the guys that they have over there on defense and the prep, I mean, it's going to take a lot of a lot of preparation, and a lot of execution," Lamb said. "We can't have as many flags because they have a really good offense, too." Prescott will lean heavily on Lamb if George Pickens misses another game. But even if Pickens plays, Prescott won't forget who he needs to target, early and often. 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey will get in the end zone twice Look for McCaffrey to score on the ground and with a reception. The 49ers are going to get him the ball near the goal line. One thing that helps McCaffrey's overall usage is that Shanahan is more confident that he is ready to rock after a pre-bye injury slowed him somewhat, according to ninerswire.com. "No. I actually forgot about it," Shanahan said. "He had a good bye week, and he told me before the bye week in Christian style not to worry about it at all. He'll be fine, and he looked good all week." McCaffrey hasn't had a blowout game all season. His rushing high is 75 yards, and his receiving high is 61. But he has 10 total touchdowns, with nine of them coming off the ground. And consistency has been a hallmark. McCaffrey has scored in seven straight games. In three of those contests, he scored twice. The 49ers will need to be sharp offensively. Despite the way their defense has played, they will have trouble slowing down the Cowboys' high-octane offense. McCaffrey will likely need those scores to keep his team in good business. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton At one time…a few decades ago…the 49ers and the Cowboys was the top rivalry in the NFL. In 2026, Sunday’s game between the 49ers (7-1) and the Cowboys (4-5) features one team contending for a Super Bowl and the other simply battling to remain in contention in an underwhelming division. The contrast extends beyond the standings is explained in the numbers: the 49ers are averaging 29.4 points per game while allowing 19.5, compared with 27.3 scored and 26.2 allowed by the Cowboys. San Francisco arrives in Arlington following a convincing 38-17 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders, a game the 49ers broke open with a turnover-fueled second half. Brock Purdy completed 17 of 25 passes for 232 yards and two touchdowns and also ran for a score, while Christian McCaffrey scored once on the ground and once through the air. San Francisco led 21-10 at halftime before Jaden Dugger returned an interception 35 yards for a touchdown on the Raiders’ first offensive play of the third quarter. That started a remarkable half in which the 49ers forced five turnovers. The Niners finished with 414 total yards, including 190 rushing, possessed the ball for more than 38 minutes. Dallas also enters the matchup following a victory, escaping Indianapolis with a 27-23 win over the Colts after trailing 23-20 with less than two minutes remaining. Dak Prescott immediately answered with a 46-yard completion to Ryan Flournoy , and Javonte Williams scored from one yard out with 1:08 remaining to put Dallas ahead for good. The Cowboys piled up 508 yards of offense to Indianapolis’ 271, with Prescott completing 21 of 34 passes for 335 yards and two touchdowns, CeeDee Lamb exploding for 10 catches and 195 yards and a score, and Williams rushing for 101 yards. But Dallas made life difficult for itself with two turnovers and 14 penalties for 153 yards. This is a rivalry that has produced some of the most memorable postseason games in NFL history, from “The Catch” in the 1981 NFC Championship Game to three consecutive NFC title-game meetings between the clubs following the 1992, 1993 and 1994 seasons. San Francisco currently owns the upper hand, leading the all-time series 21-19-1 and having won the past four meetings, including playoff victories of 23-17 after the 2021 season and 19-12 after the 2022 season. The 49ers followed those wins with a 42-10 rout in 2023 and a 30-24 victory in the most recent meeting on Oct. 27, 2024.
