home.headline: Cowboys could sign Matt Milano to address linebacker injuries after trade deadline
home.blurb: Dallas fans watched Jerry Jones stand pat at the trade deadline , and the Cowboys’ linebacker room came out of Tuesday exactly as thin as it went in. DeMarvion Overshown sat out the Week 9 win in Indianapolis with hamstring and back issues, and the 7-1 49ers are next. There is a veteran sitting by the phone. Matt Milano, the former first-team All-Pro who spent nine seasons in Buffalo, is still a free agent, and Bleacher Report’s Moe Moton named Dallas as one of his two best fits after the deadline. Dallas keeps losing its linebackers Overshown hurt his hamstring in the opener against the Giants and missed the next five games before returning in Week 7. Dee Winters, the linebacker Dallas acquired from San Francisco during the draft, went down with an Achilles strain against Green Bay in Week 6. That has left rookie Jaishawn Barham and Shemar James playing more snaps than anyone planned in the spring. The results show up on the stat sheet. Dallas allows 147.4 rushing yards per game, second most in the NFL, and 5.0 yards per carry, according to ESPN . That’s part of why the defense picked up an unflattering midseason award this week. Milano is a different player than the one who earned All-Pro honors in 2022. He posted 67 tackles and 3.5 sacks in 12 games for the Bills last season, per ESPN , but PFF gave him a 46.2 run-defense grade that ranked 81st among 88 qualified linebackers. Availability is the other question, and it cuts both ways. By our count from his game logs, Milano has missed 30 of a possible 51 regular-season games over the last three years. Overshown has already missed six of the Cowboys’ nine games this season. Dallas would be adding a linebacker with an injury history to a room that already has one. The case for him is simpler than that. He has 10 career interceptions and nine seasons of experience, and he would cost Dallas no draft capital. We looked at released veterans Dallas could add at running back and cornerback this week, and linebacker deserves the same look. At 4-5, the Cowboys can’t afford many more weeks of guessing who will be healthy behind the defensive line. A veteran who can take 25 snaps on early downs would at least give Christian Parker one less problem against the 49ers and the rest of the stretch run. home.blurb: Many fans speculated that Pickens could be on the move via a trade amid the reportedly turbulent relationship between the wide receiver and the Cowboys due to failed contract talks, but nothing materialized before the deadline on Tuesday, leaving Pickens to play out the rest of the season in a Dallas uniform. Cowboys’ George Pickens injury update after not getting traded before deadline - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Misiorowski, Schlittler win Cy Youngs Cowboys’ George Pickens injury update after not getting traded before deadline Jackson Stone, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Wed, November 11, 2026 at 8:34 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Dallas Cowboys are currently gearing up for their upcoming home game against the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. Many fans were disappointed when none of the Cowboys' trade candidates, including wide receiver George Pickens , were dealt on Tuesday before the NFL trade deadline. Now, the Cowboys have gotten the latest update on Pickens' injury status for Sunday's game against the 49ers. "Cowboys WR George Pickens (hamstring/shoulder) going through individual drills during today's practice," reported Cowboys insider Jon Machota of The Athletic on X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Pickens missed last week's game, a narrow road win over the Indianapolis Colts, with the injury, having gotten hurt in the Cowboys' recent home loss to the Arizona Cardinals the weekend prior. Meanwhile, the Cowboys will now prepare to welcome in the top seed in the NFC in San Francisco, who made a trade deadline splash of its own by acquiring wide receiver Keenan Allen from the Indianapolis Colts. The Cowboys' defense, which has been a far cry from the improved unit that fans were envisioning this year, will have its hands full in dealing with the 49ers' potent offensive attack. In any case, kickoff between the Cowboys and 49ers is set for Sunday at 4:25 pm ET from Arlington. Pittsburgh got the best of Cincy in the first meeting between these teams, winning 30-27 at home, giving it the current tiebreaker in the division. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers had one of his best games of the season, throwing for 292 yards, three scores and one pick to lead the Steelers to a win at home. Now, they find themselves as underdogs on the road out of their bye week agaist Joe Burrow and Co. The Bengals are on fire right now, knocking off the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid in Week 9 for their fourth win in a row. Burrow, who is now tied with Josh Allen in the odds to win the MVP award this season, has thrown 16 scores over the last four weeks and adding a rushing touchdown for good measure in the blowout win over Atlanta. Oddsmakers have given the Bengals the edge in this division, setting them as odds-on favorites to win it ahead of this Week 10 clash. While all the primetime games in Week 10 aren't great, this matchup on Sunday Night Football is expected to be a close one between two potential playoff teams. Steelers vs. Bengals Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Steelers +3.5 (-110) Bengals -3.5 (-110) Steelers: +150 Bengals: -180 48.5 (Over -108/Under -112) Based on these odds (Cincy -180), the Bengals have an implied probability of 64.29 percent to get the win at home. This is a tough turnaround travel wise since the Bengals were in Madrid in Week 9, but they are 2-1 at home in the 2026 season. Meanwhile, the Steelers should be fairly healthy coming out of their bye week, and they have also won four games in a row to get to the top of the AFC North. Pittsburgh won the division in the 2025 season, and with the Baltimore Ravens and Cleveland Browns both losing in Week 9, this is shaping up to be a two-team race. Cincy has a fairly easy schedule the rest of the way, which is a big reason why oddsmakers have set it as the favorite in the division. “First off, we do believe the Bengals have the strongest path to win the division,” Ty Gour, Sports Trader at Fanatics Sportsbook, told Sports Illustrated. “If you look at their schedule the rest of the way, it is quite soft. The [Kansas City] Chiefs game in Week 14 is the only game we project that they will not open as the favorite as things currently stand. They have two games against the Browns, [Indianapolis] Colts game, [Washington] Commanders game, and a Ravens game – which is a lot less daunting than it once was. So, all of those games look to be pretty bankable. “Whereas the Steelers really have a much rougher path. They've still got to play the [Denver] Broncos and the Jags (Jacksonville Jaguars). Their only real bankable wins are the [Tennessee] Titans, and then they get two Ravens games.” It'll be interesting to see if this line moves at all in the coming days, but it appears the Bengals are going to close as favorites as they look to split the season series with their AFC North rival. picks.headline: Bengals vs. Steelers opening odds for massive Week 10 showdown
picks.blurb: Bengals vs. Steelers opening odds for massive Week 10 showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL news, live updates Misiorowski, Schlittler win Cy Youngs NFL midseason awards Rex Ryan arrested Skubal suitors emerge Bengals vs. Steelers opening odds for massive Week 10 showdown Alex Frank · SB Nation Mon, November 9, 2026 at 12:05 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This is as big of a home game as it gets for the Cincinnati Bengals . It's mid-November, against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and first place in the AFC North is on the line. Both the Bengals and Steelers are 6-2 and have both won four straight games. Not to mention, these two teams have already played this season. It was in Week 3, with the Steelers winning 30-27 in Pittsburgh. Right now on FanDuel , the Bengals are 3.5-point favorites next Sunday night. The Bengals' moneyline is -200, while the Steelers' is at +168. The over/under is at 47.5. Sunday night could be an extremely physical game. It's an AFC North rivalry with sole possession of first place in the division at stake. Also, it's the Bengals and Steelers. That's all you need to know for the potential level of physicality. Pittsburgh stole the first game against the Bengals, aided by two Bengals turnovers in the fourth quarter that included Joe Burrow getting strip-sacked with the Bengals on the edge of field goal range in the final minute. The Bengals never ran an offensive play with the lead in that game, but there were some great performances from their star players. Joe Burrow was 28/37 for 282 yards and three touchdowns, Ja'Marr Chase caught nine passes for 98 yards and a touchdown, and Tee Higgins hauled in six passes for 90 yards and a touchdown. Mike Gesicki also caught a 25-yard touchdown on 4th&2 early in the fourth quarter. For the Steelers, Aaron Rodgers completed 19 of 34 passes for 292 yards and three touchdowns, while Jaylen Warren rushed for 127 yards on 17 carries. Eight different players caught a pass for the Steelers, with Darnell Washington leading the way with 67 receiving yards on three receptions. Roman Wilson, D.K. Metcalf, and Ben Skowronek each caught a touchdown for the Steelers. Rodgers currently has 1,871 passing yards and 13 touchdowns on the season, but he's also thrown six interceptions and is completing just 60.8 percent of his passes. Warren has 704 rushing yards and two touchdowns, while Washington and fellow tight end Pat Friermuth lead the Steelers with three and four touchdowns, respectively. T.J. Watt, as of Sunday night, leads the NFL with 7.5 sacks, and he also has nine tackles for loss. Cornerback Jamel Dean also has three forced fumbles. Bengals right tackle Amarius Mims held T.J. Watt off the stat sheet in that game, which bodes well going into Sunday night. The Bengals' offense scored on five of their eight drives in the first meeting in Week 3, gaining 352 yards of offense and rushing for 83 yards on 18 carries. Chase Brown rushed for 61 yards on 13 carries.

picks.headline: Bengals vs. Steelers predictions: Joe Burrow, Jaylen Warren and a 34-31 final
picks.blurb: Bengals vs. Steelers predictions: Joe Burrow, Jaylen Warren and a 34-31 final - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL news, live updates Misiorowski, Schlittler win Cy Youngs NFL midseason awards Rex Ryan arrested Skubal suitors emerge Bengals vs. Steelers predictions: Joe Burrow, Jaylen Warren and a 34-31 final (Sam Greene/The Enquirer / USA TODAY) Keegan Nickoson · Roundtable Sports Wed, November 11, 2026 at 11:53 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Joe Burrow accounts for four touchdowns for the fifth straight game Burrow is on a heater, scoring four or more touchdowns, whether throwing or running, in four straight games. In his last four games against the Steelers, Burrow has thrown 11 touchdowns and four interceptions, topping 275 yards in all four games. Interestingly, Pittsburgh is a great matchup for Burrow. The Steelers play zone coverage on 84.3% of dropbacks, according to Next Gen Stats, and Burrow is the best quarterback in the NFL against zone by completion percentage, at 74.7%. Jaylen Warren rushes for 120-plus yards Warren has become one of the league's most productive running backs this season, ranking sixth in rushing yards and first in yards per carry, at 5.9. Earlier this season against the Bengals , Warren ran for the second-most yards of his season, with 127. Two weeks ago against Cleveland, Warren topped that number with 143 yards. It was the first time all season he rushed for 100 yards in back-to-back games. The Bengals' defense has been inconsistent this season, struggling with tackling some weeks and shutting down opposing offenses and forcing takeaways in others. I think that, coming off a bye, the Steelers catch the Bengals on their back foot and feed Warren, who will have a big game. Steelers win 34-31 History is not on the Bengals' side in this matchup. After playing an overseas game, teams are 0-5 when their next game comes against a team coming off a bye. The Steelers are rested, while the Bengals are recovering from nearly a full week in Madrid. A lot is at stake in this game, with the winner taking sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Pittsburgh doesn't have much momentum, especially on offense, as its best wide receiver, DK Metcalf, has been struggling with drops lately. He has just 378 receiving yards this season and has topped 100 yards just once, with a 115-yard day against Cleveland earlier this season. Metcalf had just one catch for 4 yards on six targets against the Browns. The Steelers hit a snag at the right time, giving themselves a week to figure things out. I think the Steelers pick up a big win, halting the Bengals' momentum and getting a massive tiebreaker. Pittsburgh has done a relatively good job of keeping a cap on Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins over the last couple of seasons. Outside of Chase's massive 16-catch, 161-yard game with Joe Flacco at quarterback last season, neither has topped 100 yards in their last four meetings.

picks.headline: ‘Bring your popcorn’- Mike Tomlin makes bold prediction for Steelers-Bengals clash
picks.blurb: ‘Bring your popcorn’- Mike Tomlin makes bold prediction for Steelers-Bengals clash - Yahoo Sports Search query for Search Search News Finance More Mail NFL Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images Aryan Chadha · HITC Mon, 9 November 2026 at 11:30 am UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Premier League Scottish Football Champions League Europa League Club World Cup About our ads Mike Tomlin is expecting a blockbuster AFC North showdown between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals, backing both teams to deliver an entertaining contest with the division lead at stake. The former Steelers head coach knows exactly what this rivalry means after spending 19 years in Pittsburgh before stepping away from the role. He will now get to watch his old team from the NBC crew as the two sides prepare to meet on Sunday Night Football. Both teams enter the contest with 6-2 records and four consecutive victories, setting up a major meeting between two sides looking to strengthen their position in the AFC North. Mike Tomlin backs Steelers pass rush to challenge Joe Burrow and Cincinnati Bengals Tomlin made no secret of his excitement when discussing the matchup, admitting he would be more than happy to make the trip to Cincinnati. "It's AFC North football and you know I love that. You can airmail me right to Cincinnati," Tomlin said. He also highlighted the individual battle that could define the game, with Joe Burrow and the Bengals passing attack facing Pittsburgh's formidable pass rush. "It's good on good. Joe Burrow and that Cincinnati passing game vs T.J. Watt and the four-man rush of the Steelers…. Bring your popcorn and get your cameras ready." Pittsburgh will arrive with plenty of confidence after enjoying a bye week. The Steelers' four-game winning run includes a commanding 27-6 victory over the Cleveland Browns in their most recent outing. Cincinnati have also found their rhythm, beating the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 in Madrid. Burrow completed 82.8 per cent of his passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in that victory. However, the Bengals will have revenge on their minds after losing 30-27 to Pittsburgh during their earlier meeting this season. That defeat came during a difficult spell in which Cincinnati also suffered a second consecutive loss. Now, with both teams level at 6-2, the stakes are considerably higher. Tomlin will have a particularly interesting perspective from the NBC booth as he watches the Steelers take on a Bengals team that will be determined to settle the score on home turf. (Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images) | Getty Images Frank Platko · SB Nation Thu, November 12, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Updated Standings: Pittsburgh Steelers 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals 6-2 Cleveland Browns 5-4 Baltimore Ravens 4-5 Matchup: vs. Pittsburgh Steelers, 8:20pm EST The Bengals avoided a potential letdown game last week against the Atlanta Falcons in Spain, securing a 34-17 victory. After losing the first quarter by three points, the Bengals outscored the Falcons by 20 points for the remainder of the contest. Now riding a four-game win streak, having exceeded 30+ points in each game, the Bengals will return home for a primetime matchup with the Steelers. In Week 3, the Bengals suffered a 30-27 defeat against Pittsburgh and sit in second place now despite having the same record. Cincinnati's passing attack has been firing on all cylinders recently and Joe Burrow is hitting his stride. Over the last four games, Burrow has 16 touchdown passes while averaging over 300 passing yards. The Steelers are a Top 3 defense against the run but rank middle-of-the-pack defending the pass. The Bengals continue to struggle running the ball effectively, so they'll likely attack Pittsburgh's secondary regularly. Elsewhere, the Bengals' inconsistent run defense may be tested by Steelers' rushing attack that has totaled 148 yards and 200 yards on the ground in back-to-back games. The Bengals will need to slow down Jaylen Warren in the backfield, who has been a star this season. If the Bengals can make the Steelers one dimensional offensively, they become a much more beatable team. Matchup: vs. Cincinnati Bengals, 8:20pm EST Like their divisional counterpart, the Steelers have won their last four games to improve to 6-2, sitting atop the division by virtue of tiebreaker. Prior to last week's bye break, the Steelers defeated the Browns handedly by 21 points, their most lopsided win of the season and only their second win by more than one possession. Pittsburgh's momentum will be put to the test in a tough road environment this Sunday night with the AFC North lead on the line. The Steelers have won the turnover battle in three consecutive games. That will be an important factor for them to defeat the Bengals. Burrow has taken good care of the ball this year but did have a three-interception performance just two weeks ago. If the Steelers' defense can force a turnover or two and give their offense support with shorter fields, that will go a long way in helping them keep pace. On offense, the Steelers continue to long for better production from their pass-catchers to help unlock more downfield plays. Warren has been the team's only consistent playmaker and Rico Dowdle has ran well over the last two weeks in a complimentary role. However, D.K. Metcalf and company have been up-and-down in the passing game. In order to match Cincinnati's high-flying offensive attack, the Steelers will likely need to hit on a few explosive passing plays. Matchup: vs. Houston Texans, 1:00pm EST The Browns have now lost back-to-back games and are looking to get back on track before their upcoming bye week. In Week 9, they allowed a winnable game to slip through their grasp against the Saints, where they lost by one point in overtime. Shedeur Sanders impressed in his spot-start for Deshaun Watson at quarterback, but the Browns still struggled to run the ball and didn't start scoring much until the fourth quarter. Watson is set to return from injury to start this week versus his former team. The Texans have underwhelmed defensively this year but still have one of the league's more talented defenses, which will pose a challenge for the Browns — whose offense has struggled mightily at times this season. Houston has been vulnerable in pass coverage, allowing over 235 passing yards per game, leaving some hope that Watson can hit a downfield shot or two. The Browns will need to connect on some type of explosive plays or find a way to run the ball more effectively. Defensively, the Browns will need to bring their A game, as the Texans have prolific offensively at times in recent weeks. Last Sunday, they scored 44 points and C.J. Stroud threw five touchdown passes with nearly 400 passing yards. The Browns may be able to afford to sell out against the pass rather than the run, as the Texans rank even worse running the ball than they do. Matchup: vs. Los Angeles Chargers, 8:15pm EST The Ravens were thrashed by the Jacksonville Jaguars last Thursday night, losing by 20+ points for the third straight game. Baltimore's offense struggles hit a new low, as the team scored 10 points, gained 10 first downs and totaled just over 200 yards. With a hobbled third-string quarterback under center, the Ravens were no match for a talented Jaguars' squad. Fortunately, they will get the ultimate potential get-right matchup this coming Monday, taking on a winless Chargers team that is in disarray. Hopes for a potential offensive turnaround lie with new incoming quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who the Ravens traded for after Week 9. Brissett should provide a significant upgrade over Joe Fagnano as an experienced veteran who has proven, at the bare minimum, he can lead scoring drives and operate an offense at a competent level. Even with Brissett now under center, the Ravens need more consistency from their offensive line and breakthrough performances from veterans like Mark Andrews, Ronnie Stanley and Derrick Henry. Defensively, the Ravens have given up 30+ points in three straight weeks to three of the best offenses and quarterbacks in the NFL. They've played good halves and quarters, but the lows have been low. Coverage breakdowns and lack of impact pass rush continue to plague them. If there were ever a spot to have a convincing performance and force turnovers, this would be it. Chargers' quarterback Justin Herbert leads all quarterbacks in interceptions this season.

away.headline: Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals
away.blurb: Courtesy of Wednesday's Week 10 injury report, the Steelers saw three players, who have missed time with their respective injuries, return to practice as full participants: wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf), cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring), and cornerback Doneiko Slaughter (hamstring). Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Misiorowski, Schlittler win Cy Youngs Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals Andrew Vasquez, Steelers Wire · Steelers Wire Thu, November 12, 2026 at 3:58 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers received great injury news regarding three of their players ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengal s. Skowronek, who began his career with the Los Angeles Rams (2021–2023), also spent time with the Houston Texans (2024) before joining the Steelers in 2024. A solid wide receiver depth piece and special teams ace, Skowronek suffered his calf injury in Week 5 and has missed the past three games. Echols, who began his career with the New York Jets (2021–2024), joined the Steelers in 2025 free agency. An underrated contributor for Pittsburgh's defense last season, Echols suffered his hamstring injury during Week 6 and has missed the past two games. Slaughter, who began his NFL career with the Jacksonville Jaguars (2025), joined the Steelers on a reserve/future contract in January 2026. After a strong preseason and training camp, Slaughter was signed back to the active roster on October 10, but unfortunately suffered a hamstring injury in Week 7 and has missed the past game. The fact that Skowronek, Echols, and Slaughter were able to be full participants at Wednesday's practice gives them an excellent shot at returning in Week 10 for Sunday Night Football against the Bengals . Whether he returns to practice immediately is yet to be seen, but having everyone available would be a benefit to the offense. Defensive tackle Derrick Harmon returned to practice today but remains on the Reserve/Injured List. The Steelers have a 21-day window to either activate Harmon or he remains on the Reserve/Injured List for the remainder of the season. He was placed on the Reserve/Injured List on October 10. Harmon, the Steelers No. 1 pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, appeared in four games this year, with one start, before he was placed on the Reserve/Injured List. He has 12 tackles this season, including three solo stops and a tackle for a loss. He also has one and a half sacks and a forced fumble. In two seasons, Harmon has appeared in 16 games, with nine starts. He is credited with 39 tackles, including 14 solo tackles, as well as two tackles for a loss. He also has four and a half sacks, a pass defense and a forced fumble. "I think Michael is getting close," said McCarthy on Monday. home.headline: Bengals get encouraging news with injured starter after first practice back home from Madrid
home.blurb: Left guard Dylan Fairchild (pectoral), is the new name to monitor this week. Fairchild injured his pectoral late in last Sunday’s victory over the Atlanta Falcons. It caused him to miss the very last snap of the game. Coach Zac Taylor told reporters Wednesday that they’ll take Fairchild day-to-day. Being limited to start the week off is a positive sign. Cornerback DJ Turner II (heel) was also limited. There was a chance he wouldn’t play last Sunday, but he was able to Stay in the field for nearly the entire game. Cincinnati will likely take it easy with him until his ankle is fully healed. Defense end Cedric Johnson is notably not included in the injury report, A great sign that his ankle/foot Injury from last week is no longer a concern. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) aggravated his quad injury during Week 7 and is still week-to-week. Defensive tackle Jonathan Allen had his usual rest day. AFC Playoff Picture and Projections: Who is in, and out, heading into NFL Week 10 Steelers vs. Bengals Injury Report: Derrick Harmon starts his return from IR The Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals will square off in Week 10 of the 2026 NFL Regular season, and that means it is time for the first official injury report of the week. The Ravens can shorten the game by running. They gained 172 yards on the ground against Jacksonville last Thursday, including Justice Hill's 65-yard touchdown, but managed only 55 net passing yards with Joe Fagnano at quarterback. Brissett threw for 1,719 yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions in eight starts for Arizona before the Cardinals benched him, according to Sportsnet, so offensive coordinator Declan Doyle has a more experienced passer to pair with Henry. The Chargers need to change the shape of the game. They went 12 straight quarters and 37 offensive drives without a touchdown before Quentin Johnston's 58-yard score against Houston, according to ESPN. Omarion Hampton leads the team with 369 rushing yards, and Herbert has completed 144 of 235 passes, but his 11 interceptions lead the NFL, tied with New England's Drake Maye. Minter spent the last two seasons running the Chargers' defense and knows their staff, including coordinator Chris O'Leary, whom he mentored. That familiarity gives the Ravens a detailed read on the opposition, and the offense he now faces, run by Mike McDaniel, has produced little against anyone this season. What is the latest team news? Both teams carry questions at quarterback and in the secondary, and the statuses can change before the final injury designations arrive. What is the latest on the Chargers? Herbert is listed as questionable with an injury to the middle finger of his left, non-throwing hand. X-rays were negative, and Harbaugh said Monday that he "should be good to go." Herbert left the Texans game in the fourth quarter, and DJ Uiagalelei finished it. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey is questionable after back spasms kept him out of the Texans game. Harbaugh described him as day-to-day on Monday, according to NDTV US Sports. Cornerbacks Isas Waxter and Cam Hart and defensive lineman Justin Eboigbe all hurt ankles against Houston, and Harbaugh said the Chargers would "see how the week goes." What is the latest on the Ravens? Minter said Monday that he expects Brissett to start. Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) are on injured reserve, and Fagnano, the undrafted rookie who started against Jacksonville, has dealt with an ankle issue. Safety Kyle Hamilton is questionable with a hip injury, and Minter said he "looks fairly good." If the pass rush stays quiet, Herbert gets the time his offense has lacked. Can Brissett give the Ravens a different offense? The Ravens have had 11 days since their last game and the Chargers eight, which gives Brissett more time to learn Doyle's offense. Zay Flowers leads the team with 614 receiving yards, and the Chargers allow 27.4 points per game, tied for 28th. The Chargers' defense does rank eighth in opponent third-down rate at 34.3%, so Brissett cannot count on easy conversions. Who wins the turnover battle? The Chargers have 19 giveaways, tied for 31st, and a turnover margin of minus-seven. They turned the ball over at least twice in each of their last five games. The Ravens gave it away three times in each of their last two games, so a short field is the quickest way either offense can find points. What could move Chargers vs Ravens prediction? Herbert's final designation and McConkey's availability decide how much the Chargers can threaten a Ravens secondary that allowed 280 net passing yards to Buffalo and 242 to Jacksonville. home.headline: Ravens' Lamar Jackson's Reported Injury and Return Timeline Revealed
home.blurb: Ravens' Lamar Jackson's Reported Injury and Return Timeline Revealed - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Ravens' Lamar Jackson's Reported Injury and Return Timeline Revealed Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson was placed on IR after it was revealed that he suffered a significant thumb injury in Week 8. It was not known what had occurred officially or how long he would be out. That information has now reportedly been revealed. NFL insider Ian Rapoport has revealed that Jackson is dealing with a fractured and dislocated thumb, and he will be out for most of the rest of the regular season. The report states that Jackson will be out for six to nine weeks due to the thumb injury. He struck his hand on the helmet of a Buffalo Bills defender on the first play of the game, leading to him being ruled out. If that timeline holds, it would place the quarterback's return on Dec. 13, which is Week 14 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. With Jackson out and backup Tyler Huntley out for the season, the Ravens leapt into action to secure a veteran presence. That veteran is Jacoby Brissett. There is plenty more football left to play, but the Ravens have to start winning some games to keep things alive until Jackson can return. Misiorowski, Schlittler win Cy Youngs (Mark Konezny-Imagn Images) James Brizuela · Roundtable Sports Sun, November 8, 2026 at 3:19 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Rapoport stated that, through league sources, Jackson held a meeting with the Ravens team, and the messaging was basically to "stay alive." The quarterback has every intention of returning this season and could do so if Baltimore makes it into the playoffs. If the timeline goes past those six weeks, Jackson will presumably be back by Week 17, putting him back into action against the Cincinnati Bengals on Dec. 31. This is all just a presumption, as Jackson could need more time to heal from the thumb injury. Projections are simply that: an idea of when a player would heal from the injury. Brissett was sent over to the Ravens from the Arizona Cardinals. Baltimore gave up a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick, while receiving Brissett and a 2027 fifth-round pick. It seems like a steep price to pay for the Ravens, who now have minimal picks in the 2027 NFL Draft. Brissett is a proven veteran but fell down the depth chart in Arizona due to some early-season struggles. He does have the kind of arm and rush prowess that may fit well with the way Baltimore plays. Brissett will presumably make his debut as the Ravens starter in Week 10, as the team faces the Los Angeles Chargers. Baltimore is currently on a four-game losing streak, and they sit at 4-5. They cannot afford to lose many more games if they want to compete for a playoff spot or even secure the AFC North crown.
